$comment: Mutation arms cutting the types of package anyparse.query. Format and rules: docs/testing.md, Declared arms.

arms.name: M-ADDRESS-NO-ROOT-ANCHOR
arms.note: the root-anchored last attempt is dropped, so a node hanging directly off the module has no named ancestor to widen to and falls back to an --nth ordinal - the depth `>>` cannot express and no listing then spells

arms.name: M-ADMITS-TRUE
arms.note: every write is admitted whatever half of the scope recorded it, so a third-party write to a field NAME poisons a project candidate again

arms.name: M-BINDER-KINDS-PARAMS-ONLY
arms.note: the named-binder vocabulary collapses to the parameter slots, so a local declaration, a local function, a catch variable, a loop iterator and a case binder all stop binding their own name - a backing-field reference re-binds to whichever one shadows it and the rename rewrites it anyway

arms.name: M-BUILDMACRO-TRUE
arms.note: every type reads as carrying a build macro, so static-constant stops promoting a field a macro cannot have written

arms.name: M-COND-FRAME-CONDITION-RAW
arms.note: a branch key is the condition's raw bytes, so `#if (js)` and `#if js` stop comparing equal and two sibling regions guarding one build read as different branches again

arms.name: M-COND-FRAME-REGION-KEYED
arms.find: for (i in 0...a.length) if (a[i].branch != b[i].branch || a[i].condition != b[i].condition) return false;
arms.replace: for (i in 0...a.length) if (a[i].region != b[i].region || a[i].branch != b[i].branch) return false;
arms.note: two positions are the same branch only when they sit in the same region OCCURRENCE, so `#if a f #end #if a f #end` reads as two branches and `remove-member` deletes both declarations of a pair no build can compile

arms.name: M-COND-GAP-KEEPS-DIRECTIVES
arms.note: the mention scan reads a raw region's own directives again, so renaming a local `debug` beside `#if debug` - or one named `end` beside the region's `#end` - is refused by the directive that guards it

arms.name: M-COND-GAP-SCANS-NOTHING
arms.note: no byte of a raw region is scanned at all, so the fail-closed gate stops seeing every occurrence it exists to see and every name-driven op rewrites around such a region in silence

arms.name: M-DECLARINGFILES-EMPTY
arms.note: no type is declared anywhere, so a refusal names no file and a move reads every type as undeclared

arms.name: M-DECLSITE-SCOPEWIDE
arms.note: the owner-file pin is gone, so a declaration range comes only from the scope-wide simple name and a type sharing one with a library type has none

arms.name: M-FN-SCOPE-KINDS-DROPS-METHODS
arms.note: the METHOD half of the scope vocabulary is dropped and only the function VALUES remain, so a method body stops counting as a scope that can bind the property name and the `this.` qualifier a shadowed reference needs is never emitted

arms.name: M-FN-SCOPE-KINDS-FROZEN
arms.note: the derivation is frozen back into the hand copy it replaced - identical for the Haxe grammar and blind to every other, which is exactly the state the census is retiring

arms.name: M-HASSUBTYPE-FALSE
arms.note: no type has a subtype, so prefer-enum-abstract stops refusing a container something extends

arms.name: M-INHERITS-FALSE
arms.note: no member reads as inherited, so redundant-this stops flagging a `this.` on a base-declared member

arms.name: M-ISSUBTYPE-FALSE
arms.note: the subtype relation is empty, so redundant-upcast and unreachable-catch stop seeing the relation they report on

arms.name: M-LACKSMEMBER-FALSE
arms.note: no absence is ever provable, so field-init-in-constructor stops ranking a constant it could prove nothing about

arms.name: M-LINT-BASELINE-NO-SUBTRACTION
arms.find: for (i in 0...all.length) LintDiff.spendOwn(pool, keyOf(all[i], root, identities), messages[i])
arms.note: the multiset subtraction is gone, so every standing finding comes back as new and `--baseline` degrades to the whole-file dump it exists to replace - silently, since a delta that is too LARGE still reads as a delta

arms.name: M-MEMO-OFF
arms.note: the project index is rebuilt on every demand, so the two field rules pay for it once each per pass instead of sharing one

arms.name: M-NAME-CLASH-KINDS-NO-BINDERS
arms.note: the binder half of the ambiguity vocabulary is dropped, so a second local function of the same name no longer clashes and the local-function call set is proven complete while carrying another function's calls

arms.name: M-NAMEOUTSIDE-TRUE
arms.note: every name reads as occurring outside its excluded regions, so unused-public-member keeps every member it should have flagged (nameOccursOutside delegates here)

arms.name: M-NO-INVALIDATE
arms.note: a new --fix pass keeps the previous pass's project index, so the checks answer from sources the pass already rewrote

arms.name: M-PATHWALK-NULL
arms.note: a member path resolves to nothing, so comparison-to-boolean stops learning the type of a field-access operand. A fragment rather than a force: the member is inline, and a forced return ahead of the body is a non-final return the compiler refuses

arms.name: M-ROOTS-THIRDPARTY
arms.note: the declared resolutionRoots are tagged third-party along with the library, so a write from a project module outside the lint scope stops vetoing

arms.name: M-SHADOWEXT-TRUE
arms.note: every member reads as shadowing a `using` extension, so prefer-count takes the qualified `Lambda.count(xs, …)` spelling and inserts no `using`

arms.name: M-SUBOVERRIDE-TRUE
arms.note: every property reads as overridden below, so trivial-getter refuses every collapse it should make

arms.name: M-SUPERDECLARES-FALSE
arms.note: no supertype declares anything, so a backing-field owner binding stops being classified through its foreign supertype

arms.name: M-UNRELATED-FALSE
arms.note: no two classes are provably unrelated, so impossible-cast and impossible-is-check stop reporting

arms.name: M-SKIPSCAN-SCOPEWIDE
arms.note: the skip-parse scan spans the whole resolution scope again, so a skip-parsing library source that merely SPELLS a project member name vetoes the candidate

arms.name: M-PLAINCLASS-SCOPEBLIND
arms.replace:
final named: Array<ResolvedType> = _index.refs.resolvedDeclsNamed(SourceText.lastSegment(path));
		final resolved: Null<ResolvedType> = named.length == 1 ? named[0] : null;
arms.note: the plain-class proof goes back to a scope-blind global uniqueness count, so a type the candidate file can neither import nor reach by package frees the candidate

arms.name: M-STRUCT-DECLARES-LOOSE
arms.note: structural conformance reads the absence walk's negation again, so an unresolvable supertype declares EVERY member and any subclass of an out-of-scope type conforms by member name

arms.name: M-STRUCT-NOMINAL-OPEN
arms.note: no written type is comparable, so the unification refutation never fires and a member SET match pins again whatever the two types are

arms.name: M-STRUCT-ALIAS-OPAQUE
arms.find:
final target: Null<String> = decl.type.aliasTargetRaw;
		return target == null || !_refs.markSeen(decl, seen) ? null : comparableTypeOf(target, decl, seen);
arms.note: a plain `typedef A = C` alias is compared as its own written name instead of being followed, so `{x:MyInt}` stops pinning a `var x:Int` the compiler does unify with it

arms.name: M-STRUCT-NULL-OPAQUE
arms.replace:
if (nominal == NULLABLE_WRAPPER_TYPE_NAME) return { name: nominal, decl: null };
		if (nominal == NULLABLE_WRAPPER_TYPE_NAME) {
arms.note: the nullability wrapper is compared as the nominal `Null`, so `{var x:Null<Int>}` stops pinning a `var x:Int` it accepts in both directions

arms.name: M-STRUCT-TYPEPARAM-CLOSED
arms.replace: if (host.type.typeParamNames.contains(nominal)) return { name: nominal, decl: null };
arms.note: a structure member typed as its declaration's own type PARAMETER is compared as an ordinary nominal, so it refutes every argument it could have bound to

arms.name: M-STRUCT-DYNAMIC-CLOSED
arms.note: `Dynamic` is compared as an ordinary nominal, so a structure member declared `Dynamic` refutes every type it unifies with

arms.name: M-STRUCT-ANON-VAR-KEY
arms.note: the type maps are keyed on the member node again, so every anon-structure `var x:T;` / `final x:T;` field reads as unannotated and the conformance refutation cannot fire on one

arms.name: M-STRUCT-UNRESOLVED-OPEN
arms.find: if (decl == null) return { name: nominal, decl: null };
arms.note: a nominal that resolves nowhere is OPEN instead of compared by its written name, which is the sound reading for an out-of-scope alias and drops every refutation resting on an unresolved spelling

arms.name: M-STRUCT-ANON-CLOSED
arms.replace: if (decl.type.isAnonStruct) return { name: nominal, decl: decl };
arms.note: a nominal naming an ANONYMOUS-STRUCTURE typedef is compared as a name, so a structure member typed by one refutes every class that could unify with it

arms.name: M-NULLABLE-WRAPPER-OPAQUE
arms.note: the shared typer no longer peels a member-transparent wrapper off a receiver, so a `Null<Map<K, V>>` receiver reads as `Null` and goes back to being a safe miss

arms.name: M-OPAQUE-REGION-BRACE-DELTA
arms.replace:
final braceRule: String = gaps.length > 0 ? source.substring(gaps[0].from, gaps[gaps.length - 1].to) : '';
if (gaps.length > 0 && braceRule.split('{').length != braceRule.split('}').length) {
arms.note: a region is reported raw only where its own brace counts differ - the refuted brace-delta rule, which drops 34 of the 59 raw regions measured over three trees

arms.name: M-COND-REGION-KINDS-HARDCODED
arms.find:
final kinds: Array<String> = shape.conditionalRegionKinds ?? [];
		return kinds.contains(kind);
arms.note: the region vocabulary goes back to three Haxe spellings hard-coded in the grammar-agnostic core - the second source of truth for the family, and an incomplete one: `ConditionalArgs`, `ConditionalType`, `CondBody`, `CondSharedBodyDecl` and `MetaCondStmt` are every one a `#if` region and none of them match

arms.name: M-OPAQUE-REGION-NONE
arms.note: no #if region is ever reported opaque, so fmt goes back to declining one in silence and the mutating ops lose their fail-closed gate over it

arms.name: M-OPAQUE-REGION-NODE-SPAN
arms.find: final region: Span = new Span(gaps[0].from, gaps[gaps.length - 1].to);
arms.replace: final region: Span = new Span(span.from, span.to);
arms.note: the quoted region becomes the whole splice node, so a tail splice names the operand BEFORE its #if instead of the directive

arms.name: M-OPAQUE-REGION-WS-GAP
arms.note: a whitespace-only gap counts as an unmodelled byte again, so the quote runs past the #end into the shared body that follows it

arms.name: M-DUP-CODE-RENAMED-BINDERS
arms.note: no name is a local binding any more, so the renamed reading normalizes nothing and degenerates into the exact one — two copies differing only in what their locals are called stop being a clone

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-REPEAT-WRITE-EFFECT
arms.note: a write takes effect where its node STARTS, so `i = Std.int(i) + 1` followed by two more reads is one value although the read inside it precedes the write

arms.name: M-WRITE-SITES-SELF-FIELD
arms.note: `this.a = …` is keyed by the self reference instead of the member it writes, so it no longer reaches a bare `a` read

arms.name: M-WRITE-SITES-MEMBER-TARGET
arms.note: a member target is not walked to its root, so `this.z = …` is a write no key names and kills an unrelated group

arms.name: M-WRITE-SITES-INDEX-TARGET
arms.note: an index target is not walked to its root, so `zs[0] = …` is a write no key names and kills an unrelated group

arms.name: M-WRITE-SITES-PAREN-TARGET
arms.note: a parenthesised target is not walked to its root, so `(j) -= 1` is a write no key names and kills an unrelated group

arms.name: M-WRITE-SITES-CAST-TARGET
arms.note: a cast target is not walked to its operand, so `cast(a, A).z = …` is a write no path names and kills an unrelated group

arms.name: M-WRITE-SITES-MACRO-EMIT
arms.note: a write inside a macro reification, which emits code and runs nothing, counts as a write and cuts the group

arms.name: M-OPAQUE-REGION-TRIVIA-KEPT
arms.note: the quoted range keeps its leading and trailing trivia, so a comment after the `#end` closes the region quote and a space before the `#if` becomes the column the note names

arms.name: M-REGION-INSIDE-NONE
arms.note: an opaque region never reports the children it kept, so a region unbalanced only in its head is described as wholly raw again and the quote runs back over the statements the writer formats

arms.name: M-DOCSPLIT-COVERING-TOO
arms.note: the zero-width half of the doc-splitting predicate is gone, so an edit that COVERS the owner and owns what it covers is read as an insert between the doc and its declaration

arms.name: M-DOCSPLIT-BREAKLESS-TOO
arms.note: the line-break half of the doc-splitting predicate is gone, so a modifier prepended on the owner's own line is read as a declaration inserted under its doc

arms.name: M-DOCSPLIT-OWNER-ANY
arms.note: the positive criterion is gone, so an orphaned doc before the byte that CLOSES a body counts as documenting something and add-member's append is refused with a remedy it cannot perform

arms.name: M-DOCSPAN-BANNER-IS-DOC
arms.note: a docOnly caller stops requiring `/**` on the FIRST block, so a licence banner or section header reads as the declaration's own doc

arms.name: M-BODYSLOT-AUTHORED-NEVER
arms.find: final authored: Bool = finish.editEnd >= 0 && finish.editFrom <= limit;
arms.note: a construct whose end sits inside the REPLACEMENT no longer reads as authored, so bracing a body around the following statement is refused as a swallow

arms.name: M-BODYSLOT-LIMIT-EDIT-END
arms.find: return start.editEnd < 0 ? at.ends[start.pos] ?? -1 : ownedEnd(at, start.editFrom, start.editEnd);
arms.note: an inserted start is limited by the EDIT's own end rather than by the construct the replaced region owned, so a header rewritten over its own body reads as a dropped body

arms.name: M-BODYSLOT-LEAD-KEPT
arms.note: a slot whose demanding tokens the edit took away is still read as an emptied slot, so removing a whole `else` branch is refused as a reaching `if`

arms.name: M-COMMENT-HOIST-BLIND
arms.note: the carry criterion answers nothing, so an edit that hoists a comment across code it quotes verbatim is accepted

arms.name: M-COMMENT-CARRY-REFUSES
arms.replace: if (placed == null) return 'the carry declaration does not hold';
arms.note: a carry declaration the replacement does not bear out becomes a refusal instead of no verdict, so the guard stops failing open on its producer's bookkeeping

arms.name: M-BODYSLOT-TRIM-WS-ONLY
arms.note: a node span's trailing trivia is trimmed of WHITESPACE only, so a trailing line comment leaves the two sides carrying different amounts of it and an ordinary sole-catch removal becomes a refusal

arms.name: M-ARM-FRAGMENT-NONE
arms.note: the fragment matcher answers zero for every arm, so the walk that asks whether a stored cut still applies stops discriminating a live fragment from a rotted one

arms.name: M-SUPERTYPE-UNION-NOMEMO
arms.note: the supertype union is rebuilt on every ask, so a run that reads it once per finding pays a whole-index walk each time

arms.name: M-GRANT-SLOT-UNREAD
arms.note: the confinement gate stops asking the index for its @:allow answer, so the run-scoped slot the scan was hoisted into is no longer read

arms.name: M-EI-DUP-IMPL-ALLOWED
arms.find:
if (implementsClauseFor(declNN, ifaceName) != null)
return Err('class "$srcTypeName" already implements "$ifaceName" — refusing (nothing written)');
arms.note: a class that already implements the interface is extracted again, so a re-run splices a second clause and the header carries it twice

arms.name: M-EI-GUARD-FLAT-SCAN
arms.note: the clause scan stops descending into a conditional region, so a clause behind #if is invisible and the header gains a duplicate on every target the condition selects

arms.name: M-EI-IMPL-ANY-REFUSED
arms.find: if (node.kind == 'ImplementsClause') for (named in node.children) if (named.name == ifaceName) return node;
arms.note: the refusal widens from the named interface to any implements clause at all, so a class implementing something else can no longer be extracted from

arms.name: M-WILDCARD-REPOINT-NONE
arms.find: final statics: Array<String> = [for (m in prep.moved) if (m.isStatic) m.name];
arms.note: a caller that reached the moved static as a bare name through the source module's own wildcard import is not repointed, and the move reports Ok over a call that no longer resolves

arms.name: M-WILDCARD-BINDING-BLIND
arms.find: if (h.kind != RefKind.Decl && h.bindingSpan == null) { name: name, span: h.span, interpolated: h.interpolated }
arms.replace: if (h.kind != RefKind.Decl) { name: name, span: h.span, interpolated: h.interpolated }
arms.note: a bare read the file binds itself is treated as a wildcard reference, so a local of the moved member's name is qualified into a call

arms.name: M-WILDCARD-RIVAL-ORDER-BLIND
arms.find: src.names.contains(name) && !providers.exists(o -> o.module != srcModule && o.order > srcAt && o.names.contains(name))
arms.note: a later wildcard import providing the same name no longer wins, so a caller that never meant the source module is repointed too

arms.name: M-WILDCARD-BINDS-BLIND
arms.find: src.names.contains(name) && !providers.exists(o -> o.module != srcModule && o.order > srcAt && o.names.contains(name))
arms.replace: true && !providers.exists(o -> o.module != srcModule && o.order > srcAt && o.names.contains(name))
arms.note: the source wildcard is credited with names it does not bind, so a bare call resolved through some other import is repointed at the destination

arms.name: M-NEWFILE-IMPORT-DOUBLED
arms.note: a whole import line keeps its keyword in the path, so `@@ imports` (and add-import) refuse the statement spelling or wrap it into `import import x.Y;`

arms.name: M-NEWFILE-IMPORT-ANY-LINE
arms.note: a line that is neither a module path nor an import statement reaches assembly instead of being refused by name

arms.name: M-NEWFILE-BARE-KEYWORD-WRAPPED
arms.note: a bare `import` with no path falls through to the bare-path branch and becomes `import import;`, which parses and means nothing

arms.name: M-PATCH-COMMENT-SHAPE-CHECKED
arms.note: a comment goes back through the per-line shape check the writer's own re-guttering cannot pass, so a well-formed doc payload reads as corruption

arms.name: M-PATCH-SHAPE-ALWAYS-SURVIVES
arms.note: the per-line shape check accepts everything, so a replacement whose lines shift by different amounts inside a string literal is written

arms.name: M-ADDMETA-NO-WRAPPER-CLIMB
arms.note: the climb past a modifier wrapper is inverted, so `final class X` takes its entry inside the wrapper and the header no longer parses

arms.name: M-ADDMETA-ZERO-WIDTH-INSERT
arms.note: the entry is spliced as a zero-width insert again, so the doc-splitting guard refuses every annotation on a documented declaration

arms.name: M-LINE-DIFF-HULL
arms.note: the diff never finds a script, so it answers none for every edit and the run between two edits is never reported unchanged

arms.name: M-LINE-DIFF-PARITY
arms.find: if (x >= n && y >= m) reached = true;
arms.replace: if (x >= n && y >= m && (n - m) % 2 == d % 2) reached = true;
arms.note: the end is recognised only when the length difference and the edit distance share a remainder, which a negative odd difference never does, so a script whose new text is an odd number of lines longer is never found

arms.name: M-ADDMETA-LOOSE-WRAPPER-CLIMB
arms.find:
final outer: Null<TypeDeclMatch> = RefactorSupport.typeDeclOf(p);
if (outer == null || outer.nameNode != host) break;
arms.note: the climb asks "is my parent a single-child node" again instead of asking for a type declaration, so a #if region wrapping one type is climbed through and the entry lands above the directive

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WELD-BLIND
arms.note: the weld criterion answers for nothing, so an edit that closes two comment blocks over the code that stood between them passes the seam

arms.name: M-COMMENT-BOUNDARY-BREAK-KEPT
arms.note: a match that begins or ends on a folded line break consumes it again, so a find copied out of the normalized body runs two comment lines into one

arms.name: M-COMMENT-BOUNDARY-TRAIL-INDEX
arms.note: the trailing guard reads the needle at a NORMALIZED-body offset, which is out of range for every match past offset 0, so only the leading half of the boundary rule survives

arms.name: M-COMMENT-RUN-PER-TOKEN
arms.note: a run of contiguous full-line `//` comments stops merging into one body, so a find spanning two of its lines matches nothing and comment-rewrite reports the text absent from the file

arms.name: M-COMMENT-RUN-OPENER-UNGUARDED
arms.note: the run invariant is never checked, so a --regex replacement that deletes an interior `//` opener turns a commented-out line into live code and the op reports success

arms.name: M-COMMENT-MARKER-FORCED
arms.note: every body folds the `//` opener as its continuation marker, so a `//` line INSIDE a block comment reads as structure rather than content and a find naming it matches nothing

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-ABSENT
arms.note: the spliced body is handed back unwrapped, so a find crossing a comment line break joins the two lines and the width gate refuses the edit the join made over-long

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-GREEDY
arms.note: the reflow fills every wrapped line to the limit instead of the narrowest width costing the same lines, so a joined run comes back as a full-width line followed by a stub

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-TOUCHED-ONLY
arms.note: the reflow stops asking which lines the edit produced, so an inherited over-width doc line the caller never mentioned is re-wrapped along with the one it did

arms.name: M-COMMENT-PARAGRAPH-UNGUARDED
arms.note: a blank comment line reads as an ordinary break again, so a find spanning two paragraphs deletes the separator between them and the op reports success

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-UNSAFE-LINES
arms.note: every comment line reads as plain prose, so the reflow breaks a `// noqa: <rule>` after the colon into a blanket exemption and lays a code sample, a table row and a bullet out at the bare gutter

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-TRAILING-WRAPPED
arms.note: a `//` trailing after code is wrapped like any other, so its continuation becomes a NEW own-line comment the writer relocates — and a trailing `// noqa: <rule>` broken after the colon widens to every rule

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-COUNT-ONLY
arms.find: if (balanced.length <= lines && widestChunk(balanced, firstCols, contCols, tab) <= ceiling) return balanced;
arms.note: the balancer weighs line count alone, so it accepts the one-line answer `fillText` returns when no break point fits and a wrappable line is refused as over-width

arms.name: M-COMMENT-WIDTH-PROTECTION-BY-TEXT
arms.find: final untouched: Bool = wrapAt == null ? keep.contains(raw) : !wrapAt.contains(i);
arms.note: the index channel collapses back to matching a line by its TEXT, so two identical over-width lines in one block protect each other and the line a finding named comes back unwrapped with no reason given

arms.name: M-MOVE-SIBLINGS-FALSE
arms.note: no declaration ever reads as having siblings on both sides, so a middle declaration with a blank on exactly ONE side loses that blank and its neighbour is glued onto the previous closing brace

arms.name: M-MOVE-SIBLINGS-TRUE
arms.note: every declaration reads as having siblings on both sides, so the separator a last declaration owns is left standing at the end of its container

arms.name: M-MOVE-CUT-TAKES-BOTH-RUNS
arms.note: a cut with a blank run on both sides takes BOTH, which is right only at a real container end and glues a trailing comment onto the previous declaration's closing brace

arms.name: M-MOVE-BLANKRUN-END-NOOP
arms.note: the forward blank-run scan answers its own start, so a cut never takes the run that follows it and the removed declaration leaves a blank line behind

arms.name: M-MOVE-FQN-COMMENT-MASK-NONE
arms.note: the fully-qualified-path scan reads comments as code again, so a prose line naming the old path refuses a legitimate move

arms.name: M-MOVE-FQN-ALIAS-RAW
arms.note: an alias statement's own span stops being excluded, because `raw` is the ALIAS, so `import p.A.Foo as F;` reads as a fully-qualified code reference and refuses the move

arms.name: M-MOVE-ALIAS-SUFFIX-DROPPED
arms.note: a repointed alias import loses its binding suffix, so a file that only ever names the type through the alias is left with no binding for it

arms.name: M-MOVE-NAMESCAN-COMMENT-COUNTED
arms.note: a comment INTERIOR counts as a reference again, so a doc block naming the moved type buys it a repair import no code asked for

arms.name: M-MOVE-NAMESCAN-FULLSTOP-BLIND
arms.find: return names.exists(n -> OccurrenceScan.referencedUnqualifiedInRange(source, n, 0, source.length, outside, comments));
arms.note: a comment's own full stop reads as a qualifier, so a real code reference on the line BELOW a comment ending in a period stops counting

arms.name: M-MOVE-USING-MIRROR-ANY-KIND
arms.find: for (imp in destInfo.imports) if (imp.kind == ImportKind.Using && SymbolIndex.pathImportedBy(imp) == sourceModule) {
arms.note: a plain destination module IMPORT is mirrored like a `using`, so a secondary move writes the destination a statement for a type its own module now declares

arms.name: M-MOVE-RECEIVER-ANY-IDENT
arms.note: every upper-initial identifier is priced, not only a member-access receiver, so a VALUE position such as `Type.createInstance(Dep, [])` contests a destination binding it never named

arms.name: M-REMOVE-CUT-ANNOTATIONS-NONE
arms.note: the removal report counts no annotations, so a member cut that carries two `@:meta` siblings out of the file is described as if the address had named everything it took

arms.name: M-REMOVE-CUT-SUBJECT-RAW
arms.note: the removal report names the node the cursor resolved rather than the declaration the group fold removes, so a position on a modifier keyword reports `Public` and says nothing about the member that left

arms.name: M-PFF-CALLSCAN-ALWAYS
arms.note: every binding reads as having a method called on it, so the abstract-rebind suppression runs on bindings nothing calls and prefer-final / prefer-final-field stop suggesting on a plainly never-reassigned one

arms.name: M-PFF-STDLIB-SAFE-NONE
arms.note: an unresolved declared type is assumed to rebind `this`, so the final-safe stdlib whitelist stops rescuing an Array / String / Bytes binding a method is called on

arms.name: M-PFF-REBIND-UNRESOLVED
arms.note: the index is never asked whether the declared type rebinds `this`, so a resolved CLASS type and a ctor-only abstract both fall through to the whitelist and get suppressed as unprovable

arms.name: M-SCOPE-LIBRARY-DROPPED
arms.note: the resolution scope carries only the report half, so a library type is unresolvable again and a check reading the index answers as if no scope had been configured

arms.name: M-SETMOD-MODULE-BY-TYPE-KINDS
arms.find:
final regionKind: Null<String> = shape.conditionalMemberKind;
	for (i in 1...path.length - 1) if (path[i].kind != regionKind) return false;
arms.replace:
final typeKinds: Array<String> = shape.typeDeclKinds ?? [];
	for (i in 1...path.length - 1) if (typeKinds.contains(path[i].kind)) return false;
arms.note: module level is decided by RefShape.typeDeclKinds instead of by the path holding nothing but conditional regions, so an `enum abstract` member — a kind that list does not carry — is called module-level and `+public` on it is refused

arms.name: M-SETMOD-GUARDED-ANY-VISIBILITY
arms.find: for (keyword in guarded) if (keyword == name || (visibility.contains(keyword) && visibility.contains(name)))
arms.replace: for (keyword in guarded) if (keyword == name || visibility.contains(name))
arms.note: any keyword guarded by a conditional region in the run collides with a visibility change, so a region OUTSIDE the splice — ahead of the whole run, or between the run and the declaration — stops being served

arms.name: M-META-ELEMENT-ANY-COND-REGION
arms.note: every non-empty conditional region reads as an annotation element, so a `#if debug public #end` modifier region stops being the declaration's first token and an edit addressed at it no longer takes the member

arms.name: M-CUT-DOC-KEPT-BY-ANY-PREFIX
arms.find: final span: Span = withDoc && !isAnnotationElement(node) ? docExtendedSpan(source, group, regionsOf(), true) : group;
arms.replace: final span: Span = withDoc && !isDeclPrefixSibling(node) ? docExtendedSpan(source, group, regionsOf(), true) : group;
arms.note: the doc exception widens from annotations to every declaration prefix sibling, so a cursor on a bare modifier removes the member and leaves its doc block behind to document the next one

arms.name: M-QUALPATH-COMMENT-COUNTED
arms.note: a fully-qualified path written inside a COMMENT counts as a mention again, so a move is refused over a doc line — the direction the string spelling, which nothing repairs, is the refusal's actual job

arms.name: M-CARRY-CROSSING-ANY-SIDE
arms.note: every declared carry counts as crossed whether or not the comment changed sides, so an in-place rewrite that keeps its comment between the same two carried ranges is refused

arms.name: M-STRUCT-BUILTIN-BY-NAME
arms.note: a builtin structural type is matched by member NAME instead of by its whole member set, so a class declaring `hasNext` alone reads as an Iterator and its field is refused finalization

arms.name: M-USES-EXACT-ONLY
arms.note: a type named through its module path is invisible again, so a deadness census over `uses` calls a live sub-module type dead

arms.name: M-USES-TAIL-SUBSTRING
arms.note: the qualified tail is matched as text rather than on the segment boundary, so `Mod.WrapBodyOpts` answers a query for `BodyOpts` (and `my.OtherAssets` a mentions query for `Assets`)

arms.name: M-USES-QUALIFIED-DEFAULT
arms.note: the widened match becomes the default, so the rewriter arm of `CrossRename` is handed dotted paths it would splice whole

arms.name: M-COND-BRANCH-SPAN-SHARED
arms.find: collectGuardedImports(root, false, null, r -> singleBranchRegion(r, source, shape, regions) ? r.span : null, out);
arms.replace: collectGuardedImports(root, false, null, r -> r.span, out);
arms.note: every branch of one region shares its span, so a `using` in the `#if` arm reads as covering a call in the `#else` arm and the rewrite lands with no import

arms.name: M-COND-BODY-SWALLOWS-DIRECTIVES
arms.note: a branch body is bounded by the two directives' OUTER edges, so it carries its own `#if` and the next `#else` - the shape a guessed `source --range` window produces, which is the route `cond` exists to replace

arms.name: M-COND-INNERMOST-FRAME
arms.note: a branch or closing directive lands on the OUTERMOST open region instead of the innermost, so a nested region's `#end` closes its parent and the parent's branch splits at it

arms.name: M-COND-RAW-NEVER-MARKED
arms.note: every branch answers "the tree models this", so an expression-position `#if` loses its raw-span marker and `--names` prints an empty name list where the verbatim bytes were the whole answer

arms.name: M-COND-NAMES-LITERAL-TEXT-KEPT
arms.note: no kind carries literal text, so `--names` reports a string literal's content among the declarations again - and asymmetrically, since the single-quoted spelling leaks through its `Literal` segment while the double-quoted one is kept out by the quote marks its raw name happens to carry

arms.name: M-COND-NAMES-WHOLE-LITERAL-KEPT
arms.note: only the interpolating literal's text fragment is dropped, so a grammar whose WHOLE string literal carries its content unquoted in its own name slot gets that content back among its symbol rows - the half no Haxe fixture can see, since `DoubleStringExpr` keeps its quote marks either way

arms.name: M-REMOVE-MEMBER-BRANCH-BLIND
arms.note: the branch-level duplicate question answers `no collision` for every input, so two declarations of one name inside ONE conditional branch go back to being removed together at rc 0

arms.name: M-CANDIDATE-LABEL-BARE
arms.note: an ambiguity listing goes back to `<line>:<col> Kind` per candidate, so the selector that addresses one of them is withheld and `--nth` is the only way out

arms.name: M-DECL-EDIT-SPAN-UNTRIMMED
arms.note: a declaration's edit span keeps every trailing byte its raw span swallowed, so a module-level decl contiguous with the next one owns the neighbour's doc comment for reading and for editing alike

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-LOOP-TYPE-CALLEE
arms.note: an unbound upper-case receiver is no longer a TYPE and its unresolved call is not recorded, so a static call (Main.grow()) that grows the collection reaches nothing

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-LOOP-NEW-EXPR
arms.find: if (target != null) g.addEdge(from, target, New, null, file, span);
arms.note: a constructor call leaves no edge, so a constructor that grows or replaces the collection runs behind an element binder unseen

arms.name: M-LINTDIFF-RULE-SUMMARY-BLANK
arms.note: the per-rule breakdown comes back empty, so the report answers `did a rule other than mine move` with silence again and the reader is back to filtering example lines by hand

arms.name: M-LINTDIFF-NET-UNSTATED
arms.note: the headline drops the net, so the `N findings (base M)` pair can be read backwards again - the misreading that put a phantom normalization defect in the backlog

arms.name: M-LINTDIFF-SURPLUS-BY-KEY
arms.note: the added surplus counts distinct KEYS instead of occurrences, so `added - removed` stops equalling `new - base` and a finding duplicated inside one file appears to move nothing

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-TAIL-UNSEEN
arms.find: final tailCols: Int = i == last ? closerCols : 0;
arms.note: the last body line stops owing the block its closer, so a one-line doc block one or two columns over the width is measured as legal, handed back unwrapped, and the caller's width gate refuses the edit

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-TRIGGER-TAIL-UNSEEN
arms.find: final tailCols: Int = i == last ? closerCols : 0;
arms.note: the repair trigger stops counting the closer, so an edit that left a one-line doc block over the width by exactly it reads as having gained no over-width line and the body is handed back before the wrap loop runs

arms.name: M-COMMENT-PARAGRAPH-DELETION-EXEMPT
arms.note: a DELETION is exempt from the paragraph guard again, so deleting a list's first item off the blank line in front of it takes the lead's boundary with the list and glues the rest of the list onto the lead

arms.name: M-COMMENT-CONTINUATION-ALWAYS-GUTTER
arms.note: a one-line PLAIN block's continuation gains a star gutter it never had, so the reflow turns a `/* … */` banner into a starred block and the writer then keeps that star for good

arms.name: M-TRIVGET-MOVABLE-LITERAL-FALSE
arms.note: no literal is ever movable, so a ctor-init that should relocate to the field's own default (a plain single-quoted string among them, the shape `SingleStringExpr` misclassified before its `node.name` read was replaced with a children-are-all-Literal check) is treated as an external write and pushed off the clean (default, set) collapse — onto the @:bypassAccessor arm, or, once that extra write carries the count past the bypass cap, onto the inline-getter arm, which keeps the field and writes a different fix

arms.name: M-COND-NAMES-DROP-META-NAME
arms.note: a symbol row is an identifier path again, so `cond --names` reports a metadata ARGUMENT and hides the annotation that decides what the argument means — the S188 asymmetry, and the answer a grammar declaring no `metadataNamePrefixes` still gets

arms.name: M-INERT-REGIONS-HARDCODED-KINDS
arms.note: the two kind vocabularies go back to Haxe ctor names spelled inside the grammar-agnostic masker, so the mask no longer follows the DECLARATION: a shape naming nothing inert still gets its literals masked

arms.name: M-LIT-CONTENT-KINDS-SEGMENT-ONLY
arms.note: the content vocabulary shrinks back to the interpolating literal's text segment alone — the one kind `apq lit` used to hardcode — so a query over a scope holding the same needle in both quote spellings prints half its matches and says nothing about the other half

arms.name: M-LIT-DELIMITERS-IGNORED
arms.find:
final hit: Bool = matches(n, target, exact)
					|| content != null
					&& matches(content, target, exact)
arms.replace: final hit: Bool = matches(n, target, exact)
arms.note: the declared quotes stay on the name slot for the compare, so `--exact` can never match content written in the grammar's whole-span string spelling and the two spellings answer differently again

arms.name: M-LIT-CONTENT-KINDS-FROZEN
arms.note: the content vocabulary freezes into this grammar's ctor names again - wide enough to pass every fixture that reads the Haxe shape, which is why review found the derivation itself unpinned, and no longer read from the declaration at all

arms.name: M-INERT-SEGMENT-KINDS-HARDCODED
arms.note: the inert segment kinds go back to Haxe ctor names inside the agnostic masker - the THIRD vocabulary of this class, the one the multi-pair arm on `collectLiterals` does not reach - so the segment split no longer follows the declaration

arms.name: M-TRIVGET-NO-NEGATION-DESCENT
arms.note: the one-level descent into the grammar's negation node goes away, so a written negative default (`-1`, `-1.5`) is read as an operator rather than as the literal it projects and the ctor-init is pushed onto the @:bypassAccessor arm - the exact asymmetry review measured beside a byte-equivalent `255`, which folded clean

arms.name: M-TRIVGET-INERT-SEGMENT-IGNORED
arms.note: the declared inert segments of an interpolating literal stop counting as text, so a lone-dollar and an escaped-dollar literal read as references and a ctor-init spelling either is treated as an external write - the fail-closed answer the grammar no longer needs, now that it names the two

arms.name: M-SAFE-KINDS-SUFFIX-STUB
arms.note: the retired name-convention widening comes back, readmitting every projected kind whose spelling ends in Lit / StringExpr - the regex and object literals among them, neither declared a constant by any grammar vocabulary - and `Inline`, which DUPLICATES an initializer it is told is side-effect-free, again turns one EReg into two and one empty object literal into two

arms.name: M-PURE-ARG-ROOT-ONLY
arms.note: the argument walk stops at the ROOT, so `1 + f()` is pure because `Add` is - the call under it is never seen - and an argument that allocates or calls gets DUPLICATED once per use of the parameter it substitutes; the kind vocabulary this arm used to widen is already cut on the MemberKinds side by M-SAFE-KINDS-SUFFIX-STUB

arms.name: M-PLAIN-LITERAL-FROZEN
arms.note: the shared literal predicate freezes into this grammar's ctor names - wide enough for every fixture that reads the Haxe shape, which is why the derivation needs a vocabulary the engine cannot have frozen to be proved at all

arms.name: M-PLAIN-STRING-VALUE-NO-DELIMITERS
arms.note: the declared quote characters stop being read, so a whole-span string literal's value comes back WITH its quotes - the arithmetic three consumers used to spell themselves, one of them assuming a one-character quote

arms.name: M-PATCH-DOCEND-SHIFTS-EVERY-EDIT
arms.replace: for (edit in sorted) shifted += edit.text.length - (edit.span.to - edit.span.from);
arms.note: the watched doc block's end is moved by EVERY edit of the payload, including the ones lying after it, so a multi-pair call whose pairs each apply alone is refused as a doc transfer inside a window of first-pair growths

arms.name: M-PATCH-DOCEND-NEVER-SHIFTS
arms.note: the watched doc block's end is never moved, so a payload whose earlier pair grows ahead of that block leaves the guard looking for the doc before where it now is and a real transfer goes through

arms.name: M-PATCH-STRADDLED-DOC-UNWATCHED
arms.replace: if (doc == null || seen.contains(doc.to) || sorted.exists(e -> e.span.from < doc.to && e.span.to > doc.to)) continue;
arms.note: the retired `-1` answer comes back as a skip: a payload whose first pair rewrites the watched doc block drops the watch altogether, so a second pair pushing a declaration in under that block transfers the doc at rc 0

arms.name: M-PATCH-ENCLOSING-DOC-UNWATCHED
arms.note: an edit starting inside a doc block watches whatever the enclosing type's doc is instead, so a fragment opening on the doc's closing line and inserting a declaration under it moves the doc at rc 0

arms.name: M-PATCH-SPLICED-DOC-START-UNREAD
arms.find: final starting: Null<{ from: Int, to: Int, isLine: Bool }> = comments.find(t -> t.from == from && isDocBlock(source, t));
arms.replace: final starting: Null<{ from: Int, to: Int, isLine: Bool }> = null;
arms.note: the watched block's spliced end is no longer read off the doc token still starting where it did, so a fragment opening on the doc's closing line maps that end past the whole replacement and the declaration it inserts under the doc takes it at rc 0

arms.name: M-PATCH-SPLICED-DOC-OPENING-UNREAD
arms.replace: final tok: Null<{ from: Int, to: Int, isLine: Bool }> = starting;
arms.note: a doc whose opening another pair rewrote is no longer found by the token its moved start falls inside, so the arithmetic end lands past the second pair's replacement and a declaration that pair inserts under the doc takes it at rc 0

arms.name: M-PATCH-NEW-OWNER-PREDECLARED-UNCHECKED
arms.find: final took: Bool = siblingDeclares(tree, w.node, now, shape) || siblingDeclares(tree, top, now, shape);
arms.note: a doc whose new owner was already declared in the container reads as a rename, so deleting the documented declaration leaves its doc on the next one at rc 0

arms.name: M-PATCH-GROWTH-COUNTED-CONTAINER-WIDE
arms.find: final grew: Bool = w.declared >= 0 && declsInRegion(after, owner, new Span(docEnd, w.ownerEnd)) > w.declared;
arms.replace: final grew: Bool = w.declared >= 0 && declsInRegion(after, owner, new Span(0, spliced.length)) > w.declared;
arms.note: the growth is counted over the whole container again, so a pair renaming a documented member and a pair inserting anywhere else in the same container are refused together as a doc transfer that never happened

arms.name: M-SELECT-MISS-NO-KIND-CLAUSE
arms.note: a `--select` miss explains only where the NAME lives, never that the KIND is one no rule of the grammar projects, so a misspelled kind reads exactly like a declaration that is somewhere else

arms.name: M-PAREN-FREE-ROOTS-ATOMS-ONLY
arms.note: the wide root vocabulary stops reading maximalPrecedenceRootKinds and collapses onto the self-delimiting atoms, which is the engine deciding a precedence question the grammar declares: a call / field read / index / `new` substituted by inline-method gets a parenthesis it does not need, and no other fixture sees the difference

arms.name: M-SIDE-EFFECT-FREE-DROPS-OPERATORS
arms.note: the declared pure operators stop reaching the side-effect-free vocabulary, so every operator expression becomes impure: `inline` refuses an `a + b` initializer it used to substitute, and the 25 operator names go back to being unreachable from any declaration

arms.name: M-SUBTYPE-KEY-SIMPLE-NAME
arms.note: the declaration-keyed subtype bucket collapses back onto the simple-name one, so a supertype reference that resolves to ANOTHER package's namesake is attributed to every declaration of that name again - the twin named like a library class loses its prefer-inline finding, its private constructor stays shielded and its enum-abstract conversion stays refused

arms.name: M-KIND-CLAUSE-POOL-GRAMMAR-ONLY
arms.note: the did-you-mean pool shrinks back to the grammar's own vocabulary, so a caller-minted kind stays ADMITTED but unreachable: `--kind Coment` is refused with no spelling named, which is the half of a fail-closed gate that decides whether the refusal helps

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-IMPORT-BAND
arms.note: every explicit binding is weighed against the tiers below it as if it held in one build only, so the precedence collapses: an explicit import no longer outranks a wildcard one, the module's own statements no longer outrank the chain, a nearer ambient source no longer outranks a farther one, and an ambient binding no longer outranks a same-package namesake

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-GUARDED-UNION
arms.find: final guarded: Bool = imp.guarded && !coGuarded(imp, fi, order.use);
arms.note: no explicit statement is ever seen as `#if`-guarded, so the engine pins the declaration ONE build resolves where the builds disagree

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-UNPARSED-EMPTY
arms.note: an ambient source that does not parse is reported as binding NOTHING instead of as unknown, so the reader stays pinnable against a chain member the engine could not read

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-ALIAS-PINNED
arms.note: a written supertype the file binds as an ALIAS is pinned to whichever same-named declaration package proximity picks, and the declaration the alias really names loses its shield

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-CHAIN-STALE
arms.note: the memo of a directory chain and of the import maps keyed by path survives a pass that rewrote an ambient source, so every later pass of one --fix run resolves against the tree that was while the plugin behind the decorator reads disk fresh

arms.name: M-IMPORT-LEAF-ONLY-NAMES
arms.note: an import statement is read as binding its LEAF name alone, so a statement naming a module stops carrying the siblings that module declares and both import rules decide a name they never look at

arms.name: M-FIAD-PUBLIC-ADMITTED
arms.note: a public field (or one of a `@:publicFields` type) crosses `super(...)`, although code outside the project scope may read it early

arms.name: M-FRESH-ONLY-WRITES-ADMITTED
arms.note: a write of shared state the right-hand side's code makes is admitted, so a construction setting a static the base constructor reads moves ahead of the read

arms.name: M-FRESH-ONLY-STATEFUL-LIBRARY
arms.note: a pure library call that advances hidden state (`Math.random`) is skipped as harmless, so two draws the move reorders are taken to commute

arms.name: M-FRESH-ONLY-ENTRY-FACETED
arms.find: if (!view.faceted(g, file, span)) return Unconfined(file, span, 'the compiler facts do not describe the code');
arms.note: a right-hand side in a file the run rewrote reads as reading nothing, so the next `--fix` pass hoists an init whose static read the base constructor changes

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-NEVER
arms.note: no iterable is proved to iterate the same values, so an unread key over an Array or List is spelled `_` instead of dropped

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-ALWAYS
arms.note: every iterable counts as proved, so an unread key over a Map is dropped although its keyValueIterator reads a removed entry back as null

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-SHADOW-BLIND
arms.find: if (stdPath == null || shadowedByNonStdType(index, nominal)) return null;
arms.note: a project type named List is taken for the std one, so its key is dropped against an iterator() it may not have

arms.name: M-ULB-REASSIGNED-LOCAL-BLIND
arms.note: a local or parameter written in its scope is trusted, so a key is dropped over it and the value loop re-reads the reassigned local

arms.name: M-ULB-IMPORT-ALIAS-BLIND
arms.find: final rebound: Bool = root.children.exists(c -> aliasKinds.contains(c.kind) && c.name == nominal);
arms.note: an import alias spelling List is taken for the std List, so a key is dropped over the aliased Map

arms.name: M-ULB-IMPORT-REBIND-BLIND
arms.find: if (imported != null && imported != stdPath) return null;
arms.note: an import binding List to another module is taken for the std List

arms.name: M-FINAL-MACRO-FOLD-ADMITTED
arms.note: the null-guarded default fold is admitted on a macro-built owner under the oracle, although it turns a property into a field and moves the default after builder code, both of which compile

arms.name: M-FINAL-MACRO-FINALITY-BLIND
arms.note: a builder that reads field finality is trusted to the oracle, although `final` then compiles and generates something else

arms.name: M-REACH-OUT-OF-SCOPE
arms.note: a run that did not read every project file answers as if it had, so a toucher in an unread file is missed

arms.name: M-REACH-WALK-UNKNOWN
arms.note: the walk proves nothing, so every entry that runs code is refused

arms.name: M-REACH-TOUCHER-FOUND
arms.find:
if (!shared && touchers.exists(id) && !freshlyConstructed(g, id, step, scan, member))
					return Reached(pathTo(reach, id, touchers[id]));
arms.note: reaching a function that touches the member is not noticed, so a callee that grows the collection reads as harmless

arms.name: M-REACH-METHOD-TOUCH
arms.note: a mutating method call (items.pop()) on the member is not a touch

arms.name: M-REACH-SLOT-WRITE
arms.find: if (pk == shape.indexAccessKind && index == 0) return { touch: writes(grand, parentIndex), escape: false };
arms.replace: if (pk == shape.indexAccessKind && index == 0) return { touch: false, escape: false };
arms.note: an element write (items[0] = v) is not a touch

arms.name: M-REACH-ESCAPE-ARGUMENT
arms.note: the member's value handed out as an argument is not an escape, so an alias changed by code that never names it is missed

arms.name: M-REACH-FRESH-ASSIGN
arms.note: every stored value counts as freshly built, so a shared array assigned into the member is not an escape

arms.name: M-REACH-SHARED-INITIALIZER
arms.note: a member initialized from a shared value is not an escape

arms.name: M-GRAPH-SETTER-EDGE
arms.note: a property write leaves no edge to its setter, so the code set_x runs is invisible

arms.name: M-GRAPH-GETTER-EDGE
arms.note: a property read leaves no edge to its getter, so the code get_x runs is invisible

arms.name: M-REACH-VALUE-CHANNEL
arms.note: a method stored as a value is not admitted at a call through a function value, so cb() never reaches what cb holds

arms.name: M-REACH-NAME-CHANNEL
arms.note: a call through a Dynamic or untyped receiver admits no same-named function

arms.name: M-REACH-REFLECT-LITERAL
arms.note: Reflect.setField(this, 'items', …) is not a touch of items

arms.name: M-REACH-REFLECT-COMPUTED
arms.note: a reflective access by a computed name is not a blind spot

arms.name: M-REACH-NATIVE
arms.note: target-language code in a reached function is not a blind spot

arms.name: M-REACH-UNTYPED
arms.note: untyped code in a reached function is not a blind spot

arms.name: M-REACH-SKIP-PARSE
arms.note: a project file that did not parse and spells the member is not a blind spot

arms.name: M-REACH-SKIP-PARSE-ANY
arms.note: an unparsed project file counts only when it spells the member, so an override it declares is walked past

arms.name: M-REACH-SKIP-PARSE-LOCAL
arms.find: for (skipped in g.skippedFiles) if (_projectSources.exists(skipped)) return Unknown(SkipParse(skipped));
arms.replace: for (skipped in g.skippedFiles) if (false) return Unknown(SkipParse(skipped));
arms.note: a shared collection's region is proved although an unparsed project file may hold an implicitly-called function

arms.name: M-REACH-LIB-SKIP-OVERRIDE
arms.note: a library file that did not parse is invisible to a dispatch, so an override it declares is walked past

arms.name: M-REACH-LIB-REFLECT-TOUCH
arms.find: if (libraryTouchAt == null) libraryTouchAt = { from: from, file: file, span: span };
arms.note: a library body reading the member by name through its owner's type only admits functions of that name

arms.name: M-REACH-LIB-REFLECT-UNSURE
arms.note: a library body reading the member's name through an untyped receiver is taken for another type's field

arms.name: M-REACH-LIB-REFLECT-UNRELATED
arms.note: (precision) a library read of an unrelated type's same-named field blocks every proof

arms.name: M-CARRY-SUBTYPE-MEET
arms.note: a value's types are its static type alone, so two types only a common subtype relates read as unrelated

arms.name: M-CARRY-CLASSPATH
arms.note: a type's subtypes are the index's even when the builds compile code the index does not hold

arms.name: M-CARRY-ESCAPES
arms.note: a value's types are its static type's alone, so an instance that left the type system through a Dynamic or a cast is never the object an unrelated receiver holds

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-STORE
arms.note: a value assigned into a Dynamic field or variable stays typed

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-CAST
arms.note: an unchecked cast keeps its operand's type, so `me = cast this` into an unrelated type is not an exit

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-DECL
arms.note: a declaration annotated Any or Dynamic keeps its initializer typed

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-PARAM
arms.note: every parameter keeps what it is handed typed, a Dynamic or rest one included

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-RETURN
arms.note: a value returned from a function declared Dynamic stays typed

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-LAMBDA
arms.note: an arrow lambda's result is not an exit, though the function type it is handed to says nothing of it

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-THROW
arms.note: a thrown value stays typed, though a catch may bind it as Dynamic

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-METHOD-VALUE
arms.note: a method read as a value carries no object, though a bound method holds its receiver

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-HELD
arms.note: an escaped object's fields stay typed, though code holding it untyped reads them by name

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-LIBRARY-SUPER
arms.note: a class inheriting library code keeps its instances typed, though that code runs with the instance as its own this

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-NATIVE
arms.note: target-language and untyped code in the project reaches no object, though it sees every local and static by name

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-NAMED-CLASS
arms.note: a class named to the class-value producer, or any class under a computed name, is never built untyped

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-ANY
arms.find: ? { types: out, raw: false, ids: null } :
arms.replace: ? { types: null, raw: false, ids: null } :
arms.note: (precision) every instance may be anywhere, so no receiver ever rules out an owner

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-STORE
arms.note: (precision) a value stored in a typed place is an exit

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-CAST
arms.note: (precision) a runtime-checked cast is an exit, though it throws on a wrong type

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-THROW
arms.find:
// a catch may bind what is thrown as a catch-all
				value(first);
arms.replace:
// a catch may bind what is thrown as a catch-all
				ok = false;
arms.note: (precision) any thrown value leaves every instance anywhere, a string included

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-DECL
arms.note: (precision) an initializer of a declaration annotated with a class is an exit

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-PARAM
arms.note: (precision) a value passed to a class-typed parameter is an exit

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-RETURN
arms.note: (precision) a value returned from a function declared with a class is an exit

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-LAMBDA
arms.note: (precision) any arrow lambda leaves every instance anywhere

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-METHOD-VALUE
arms.note: (precision) a static method read as a value is taken to carry an instance

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-HELD
arms.note: (precision) an escaped object with any field leaves every instance anywhere

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-LIBRARY-SUPER
arms.note: (precision) every class is taken to inherit library code

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-NATIVE
arms.replace:
case ReflectiveName(_), ArrayChange:
				return { types: null, raw: false, ids: null };
arms.note: (precision) an array change or a literal reflective name in the project leaves every instance anywhere

arms.name: M-ESCAPE-P-TYPED-ARGS
arms.note: (precision) a container of a class is untyped, so an Array<C> holding this is an exit

arms.name: M-FACTS-GENERIC-RANGES
arms.note: a generic instance copy claims its generic class ranges

arms.name: M-FACTS-STALE-FOREIGN
arms.note: a spliced fact lost to a dropped file leaves no mark

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-EDGES
arms.find: return truth || contextAlike(g, node, outer) ? outer : null;
arms.note: no function is read through its compiler facts, so a call the syntax cannot resolve is admitted by name again

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-OVERRIDES
arms.find: for (v in view.overrides(g, dispatch, name)) if (!targets.contains(v)) targets.push(v);

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-VALUE

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-SPLICE
arms.replace:
case InlineSite: false;
			case MacroExpansion: true;

arms.name: M-FACTS-TRUTH-SPLICE
arms.note: (precision) under the whole list of builds a body an inlined function was spliced into keeps its syntax, which admits every conversion in play

arms.name: M-FACTS-TRUTH-SPLICE-ALWAYS
arms.note: a body an inlined function was spliced into is read through its facts with no list of builds, where a range question cannot take the spliced facts

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPLICED-WITHIN
arms.note: (precision) a range question under the whole list of builds is Unknown in a body an inlined function was spliced into, so its syntax answers

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPLICED-WITHIN-UNPLACED
arms.find: splice && spliced && !FactSites.placed(n, where) ? runsIn(n, where, span, dropped) : whole || inside(key, span, where)
arms.note: a range question in a body an inlined function was spliced into drops the spliced facts, which sit at the callee yet run in the body

arms.name: M-FACTS-TRUTH-SITES-SPLICED
arms.find: n -> n.strings, s -> s.at, truth, harmless
arms.replace: n -> n.strings, s -> s.at, false, harmless
arms.note: the implicit-call sites of a region in a body an inlined function was spliced into are read off the syntax under the whole list of builds

arms.name: M-FACTS-TRUTH-HAZARDS-SPLICED
arms.find: n -> n.natives, f -> f.at, true, harmless
arms.replace: n -> n.natives, f -> f.at, false, harmless
arms.note: (precision) the hazards of a region in a body an inlined function was spliced into are read off the syntax under the whole list of builds

arms.name: M-FACTS-TRUTH-REFLECTION-INLINED
arms.note: a reflective call inlined into a faceted body is lost: the facts hold no reflective call, and the syntax misses one under another name

arms.name: M-REACH-TRUTH-SPLICED-SEEDS
arms.note: a region leaves out what an inlined body spliced into its function runs, which the facts place at the callee

arms.name: M-GRAPH-FACTS-SPLICED-SITE
arms.find: at.file == view._table.keyOf(node.file) && FactSites.placed(n, at) ? at.span : null
arms.note: a spliced fact files its edge under its caller's file at the callee's range, which a region or a dead branch there then claims

arms.name: M-GRAPH-FACTS-SPLICED-FILE
arms.find: for (file in g._entries.keys()) if (view._table.keyOf(file) == key) return file;
arms.note: a function spliced in from another file is looked up in its caller's file, where no graph node starts at its range

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPLICE-SITES-MET
arms.note: (precision) what an inlined call spliced in runs in every range its caller meets, wherever the call stood

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPLICE-UNATTRIBUTED
arms.note: a spliced fact no inlined call's body holds runs nowhere, though it may run anywhere in its node

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPLICE-HARMLESS
arms.note: (precision) what a method that runs no project code spliced in is its caller's own code, the target code its body spells among it

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPLICE-INNERMOST
arms.note: a fact two declared ranges hold is attributed to the first splice, not the innermost, and runs at that splice's sites

arms.name: M-FACTS-SPLICE-SECOND-SITE
arms.note: a method inlined at two sites of a node runs what it spliced in at the first alone

arms.name: M-GRAPH-FACTS-SPLICE-HARMLESS
arms.find: if (inlined == null && splice != null && view.harmlessSplice(g, splice.callee)) return;
arms.note: (precision) the edges and sites a method that runs no project code spliced in are its caller's own

arms.name: M-GRAPH-FACTS-SPLICE-TAG
arms.find: for (i in edges ... g.edges.length) g.edges[i].spliced = where;
arms.note: an edge filed off a spliced body says nothing of where it runs: every region meeting its function takes it, and it is asked at no range

arms.name: M-GRAPH-FACTS-INLINED-SITE
arms.note: (precision) an inlined call runs anywhere in its caller, not where it was called

arms.name: M-REACH-SPLICED-SITES
arms.find: sites == null || sites.exists(s -> spans.exists(r -> s.from < r.to && r.from < s.to))
arms.note: (precision) a region takes what a splice anywhere in its function runs

arms.name: M-REACH-SPLICED-BENIGN
arms.note: (precision) an edge a callee's splice files is asked in the callee, where it has no range, instead of where the spliced body is written

arms.name: M-REACH-SPLICED-CULPRIT
arms.find: e.spliced == null ? benignCall(g, tree, source, fn, target, call, region) : benignWhereWritten(g, e)
arms.replace: benignCall(g, tree, source, fn, target, call, region)
arms.note: (precision) an edge a splice in the region files is asked in the region, where it has no call, instead of where the spliced body is written

arms.name: M-REACH-WHERE-WRITTEN-RANGE
arms.note: (precision) a spliced edge is asked in the method it is written in at no range of it

arms.name: M-REACH-REWRITTEN-TRUTH
arms.note: a build macro whose output the facts show is the text keeps its type Unknown under the truth too, so no question about a class under an ancestor's `@:autoBuild` is ever answered

arms.name: M-REACH-REWRITTEN-UNTRUE
arms.note: the facts of listed builds retire a build macro though the list is not every build, where one it does not name may run the macro to other effect

arms.name: M-REACH-TEXTUAL-ALWAYS
arms.find: return site != null && ids.length > 0 && g.types.declarationCount(type) == 1 && textual(g, type, [site.file], ids);
arms.note: every type is its text, so a body a build macro rewrote to touch the member is read by its syntax, which never names it

arms.name: M-FACTS-OWNER-IDS
arms.note: a typed type holds no body, so a body a build macro rewrote is never asked whether it is its text

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-FIELDS-ANY
arms.note: a field declared as anything the text declares it as is alike, so a variable a macro made a property is read as the text's plain variable

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-SPELLED
arms.note: a field access on text that does not spell it is the text's, so a body a macro put at the old body's range is taken for the text

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-CALLS-ANY
arms.note: every call is the text's wherever it sits, so a body a macro put at the old body's range calling what the text never names is taken for the text

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-EXPANSION
arms.note: code an expression macro built, in no range of the text, is never the text's, so every type whose code calls such a macro — the client's `t(...)` — keeps a build macro over it Unknown

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-EXPANSION-BODY
arms.note: an expression macro the body itself calls built nothing of the text's

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-EXPANSION-SPLICED
arms.note: an expression macro an inlined method calls built nothing of the text's

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-LITERAL
arms.note: a construction at a regex or map literal spells no class, so a type holding one is not its text

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-ABSTRACT-NEW
arms.note: a construction of an abstract spells its implementation class, which no text names

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-PURE-CALL
arms.note: a call of a function that runs no project code the compiler makes for `is` is no text's

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-CONVERSION-CALL
arms.note: a conversion the compiler calls for a concatenated value is no text's

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-ACCESSOR-NAME
arms.note: an accessor called by its own name is read as a property access the text does not spell

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-JOINED-SPLICES
arms.find: ? spliced(p.span.to) || siteSpells(n, p, p.span.from, p.span.to, member, body) || accessEnds(n, p.span.to, member)
arms.replace: ? siteSpells(n, p, p.span.from, p.span.to, member, body)
arms.note: a range the compiler joined from two inlined bodies is no text's

arms.name: M-GRAPH-ADOPT-NONE
arms.note: a method a build macro made or placed outside its type's file is no node of the graph, so what its facts show it touching is never found

arms.name: M-GRAPH-ADOPT-UNRECORDED
arms.note: a method a build macro made is a node with no facts recorded, so neither what it runs nor what it touches is seen

arms.name: M-TOUCH-ADOPTED-SYNTAX
arms.note: a body a build macro placed outside its type's file is left to its text, which holds none of it, so its touch is only a guess

arms.name: M-TOUCH-ADOPTED-UNREAD
arms.note: a method a build macro made whose facts do not say how it names the member touches nothing, though no text holds it to read instead

arms.name: M-REACH-ENTRY-REWRITTEN
arms.find: if (facts == null || !facts.truth || tree == null) return null;
arms.replace: if (facts == null || tree == null || true) return null;
arms.note: an entry in code a build macro replaced is read as its text, which is none of what runs

arms.name: M-REACH-ENTRY-MEMBER
arms.note: a member question's region in code a build macro replaced is read as its text, which is none of what runs

arms.name: M-REACH-ENTRY-LOCAL
arms.note: a local question in code a build macro replaced is read as its text, which is none of what runs

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-ESCAPE-TYPED
arms.note: an escaping value is typed by the declarations alone, so one only the compiler types makes every instance escape

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-TOUCH-TYPED
arms.find: final typed: Null<String> = at == null ? null : g.facts?.view.typeSourceAt(g, file, at);
arms.note: a receiver the declarations do not type may be anything again, although the compiler typed it

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-MACRO
arms.find: truth && g != null && faceted(g, file, n.at.span) ? null : Reification(file, span);
arms.note: a macro's expansion is no blind spot, so the code it adds is never accounted for

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-DROPPED
arms.note: a table missing a configuration is read as if it held every build

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-REFLECT-VALUE
arms.find: for (r in n.reflection) if (r.isValue && meets(r.at.span, span)) return DynamicName(file, r.at.span);
arms.note: a reflective member read as a value is no blind spot, so the member it later reaches by name is never accounted for

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-BUILDS
arms.note: a build macro only the compiler saw applied never makes a type Unknown

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-GENERIC
arms.note: a @:generic instance is named by its own generated type, which no declaration holds, instead of its generic class

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-NATIVE-IDENT
arms.note: a call of a native identifier records nothing, so what it may run is never admitted

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-CONSTRUCTION
arms.note: a construction the facts record never runs the initializers of a generated constructor

arms.name: M-GRAPH-LOCAL-INLINE
arms.note: a local inline function is no node of the graph, so a call of it resolves to nothing and what it runs is never walked

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-BIND
arms.note: a closure the compiler made is dropped, so the method a bound call runs is never used as a value

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-ALIKE
arms.find: var answer: Bool = typeAlike(owner) && declaredAlike(owner, name, true);
arms.note: a member whose declaration some build types differently is trusted as the listed builds typed it

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-GUARDED-NAME
arms.find: for (name in statics) if (guarded.exists(name)) return false;
arms.note: a call naming a member some build declares conditionally is trusted, though that build resolves it to the member

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-NESTED-OWNER
arms.find: if (owner != null && owner.id != node.id && owner.span.from == n.at.span.from) return null;
arms.note: a function with no typed body of its own is read through the facts of a function nested in it, which leave out what it runs itself

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-SYNTAX-UNION
arms.note: a faceted function records the facts' edges alone, so a name another build resolves the way the syntax reads it is lost

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-GUARDED-IMPORT
arms.find: if (guarded || conditional(text.file, text.source, header)) answer = false;
arms.note: a type in a file importing under a condition is trusted as the listed builds typed its members

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-LIBRARY-DYNAMIC
arms.note: a call of a library dynamic method the graph has not read records no edge, so its body is never read

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-UNREAD-VALUE
arms.note: the value channel is taken to run only code the walk enters, so a stored function's conversion is never admitted

arms.name: M-REACH-ABSTRACT-TEXT-ANY
arms.note: an abstract's own toString is taken to run on the abstract alone, though it may convert the value it wraps

arms.name: M-GRAPH-USING-META
arms.find: final bringing: Null<String> = g.types.firstOnChain(recv.typeName, t -> g.types.meta.bringsExtensions(t));
arms.note: a call no member declares resolves to the extensions the file's `using`s name, though a `@:using` on the receiver's type may supply another

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-USING-META
arms.note: a function naming a type that brings extensions in is read through the facts, which name the extension the listed builds resolved

arms.name: M-INDEX-GUARDED-META-LIFT
arms.find: final held: Array<QueryNode> = node.name == null ? [for (c in node.children) if (isMetaNodeKind(c.kind)) c] : [];
arms.note: metadata a conditional region holds alone is lifted nameless, so the declaration it annotates carries none of it

arms.name: M-FACTS-REACH-UNREAD-IMPLICIT
arms.note: code the walk never enters, read by its syntax, is taken to run no operator, index or literal member, only conversions and iterations

arms.name: M-FACTS-SOLE-MEMBER-NONE
