arms.name: M-FACTS-SOLE-MEMBER-DECLARED
arms.note: a declaration of the member no build typed, which may run under another name, leaves the name one type's member

arms.name: M-ADMIT-SYNTAX-READ-UNTRUE
arms.note: facts that are not the truth narrow what code the walk never enters runs implicitly

arms.name: M-ADMIT-SYNTAX-READ-FACETED
arms.note: a function value read by its syntax is taken to run implicitly only what code read through its facts does

arms.name: M-ADMIT-SYNTAX-READ-UNSEEN
arms.note: library code the walk has not read is taken to run implicitly only what code read through its facts does

arms.name: M-ADMIT-SYNTAX-READ-FIELD
arms.note: (precision) a project field holding a function value counts as library code not read, so the facts never narrow a stored function's call

arms.name: M-REACH-UNREAD-NARROWED
arms.note: (precision) code read through facts that are the truth is taken to run any implicitly-called member, as code read by its syntax may

arms.name: M-REACH-UNREAD-RECHECK
arms.note: a narrowed unread admission is never widened once the graph grows to hold code read by its syntax or not read at all

arms.name: M-REACH-TYPED-IMPLICIT-TEXT
arms.note: code read through its facts is taken to convert nothing to a string without a call the graph holds

arms.name: M-REACH-TYPED-IMPLICIT-ITER
arms.note: code read through its facts is taken to iterate nothing without a call the graph holds

arms.name: M-REACH-ITERABLE-RETURNS
arms.note: (precision) the element an iterator's `next` returns is iterated in turn, so an iterator of a type the index does not declare runs any `next`

arms.name: M-SITES-THROW-TEXT
arms.note: a `throw` is no string-conversion site of what it throws

arms.name: M-FACTS-ABSTRACT-CTOR-NAME
arms.note: a call of an abstract's constructor names `_new`, which no type the graph holds declares, so every `new` of an abstract is an unresolved dispatch

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-LITERAL-FLAGS
arms.note: a regular expression written with flags is no construction the text writes: the compiler's position of it leaves them out, so openfl's `TextField` is not its text

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-TRUTH-FACTS
arms.replace: if (view != null && view.truth && false) return factsAnswer(view);
arms.note: under the truth the escapes are still read off the project's syntax, which counts every value handed to library code as escaped

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-REFLECTION-INLINED
arms.note: any reflective body spliced in is taken to produce a class from a name it lost, so the escapes are never known

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-FLOW
arms.note: a value flowing into a catch-all, a type parameter, a structure or through a cast is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-HANDED
arms.find: for (h in n.handed) if (!typeParameter(h.to) && !escape(h.from)) return false;
arms.note: a value handed to target code is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-CLOSURE
arms.note: the receiver of a method read as a value is taken to stay in the type system, though the bound function carries it

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-DYNAMIC-RECEIVER
arms.note: the receiver of a field reached by name in untyped code is taken to stay in the type system, though any of its fields may be read

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PRODUCED
arms.note: a class a class-value producer names is taken never to be instantiated untyped

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-INSTANCES
arms.find:
if (fact != null && fact.params.length == args.length) for (i => name in fact.params)
				bindInstance(out, '$id.$name', args[i]);
arms.note: a type written with arguments binds nothing, so a value a generic class lets go is of no type

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PARAMETER
arms.find: if (bound != null) for (x in bound) if (!escapeType(x)) return false;
arms.note: a value of a type parameter is taken to be of no type, so what its instantiations bind it to never escapes

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-GENERIC-METHOD
arms.note: the instantiation of a generic method binds nothing, so a value it lets go is of no type

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-EXTENDS-EXTERN
arms.note: an instance of a class extending an extern is taken to stay in the type system, though target code runs with it as `this`

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-FIELDS
arms.find: for (f in currentFact.fields) if (f.kinds.exists(k -> k.startsWith('var(')) && !within(f.types, currentBound)) return false;
arms.note: what an escaped object's variables hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-ENUM
arms.find: case 'enum': fact.constructors.foreach(c -> constructorEscapes(id, c.name, c.type, bound));
arms.note: what an escaped enum value's constructor arguments hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-STRUCTURE
arms.note: what an escaped structure's fields hold is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-PLACE-ARGS
arms.note: a place of a nominal type is taken to keep the type of what it holds whatever its arguments, `Array<Dynamic>` included

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-TYPE-ARGS
arms.note: what an escaped container holds by its type arguments, which no variable of it declares, is taken to stay in the type system

arms.name: M-ESCAPES-FACTS-SUBTYPES
arms.note: an escaped value is taken to be of exactly its static class, never one of its subtypes

arms.name: M-REACH-EXACT-SITE
arms.find: at.exact ? exactTypes(g, t) : runtimeTypes(g, t, at.family)
arms.note: an object built right at a conversion site may be any subtype of its class, or any escaped instance

arms.name: M-FACTS-VIEW-EXACT
arms.note: the exactness the facts record of a converted operand is dropped

arms.name: M-FACTS-VIEW-EXACT-CONVERSION
arms.note: the exactness the facts record of the argument of a conversion call is dropped

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-JOINED-CONVERSION
arms.note: a conversion the compiler writes of a field read it placed across an inlined body and the text is no text's (the client's `domain.Node.parse`)

arms.name: M-FACTS-TEXT-JOINED-PLACED
arms.note: the value a field read the compiler placed across an inlined body and the text flows as is no text's (the client's `domain.Node.parse`)

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-WALK
arms.find: reachedArrayChange(g, file, tree, region, callees, shared);
arms.note: what a shared collection's region calls is admitted unwalked, so a callee growing any array proves

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-REFUSED
arms.note: every call a shared collection's region makes is a culprit again, so a region calling a pure project function is refused

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-BENIGN-EDGE
arms.note: a callee's push onto a fresh local of its own is followed into the built-in array type, whose body-less mutator refuses

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-REWRITTEN
arms.note: a callee a build macro may rewrite is read as its source

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-AMBIGUOUS
arms.note: a callee whose type name two declarations share is read as one of them

arms.name: M-REACH-CALLEE-OVERRIDES
arms.note: a dispatch on a library type reaches only the declaration, not the overrides library code declares

arms.name: M-REACH-COMPOUND-WRITE-ALIAS
arms.find: final replacing: Bool = write.kind == shape.assignKind || write.kind == shape.nullCoalAssignKind;
arms.replace:
final replacing: Bool = true;
		if (write.kind != shape.assignKind) return true;
arms.note: only a plain assignment of a shared value is an escape, so `x ??= shared` leaves `x` a fresh local whose push is taken as harmless

arms.name: M-REACH-ASSIGNMENT-VALUE-ALIAS
arms.replace: if (true) return holder.kind != shape.exprStatementKind || valueDiscarded(lineage, at - 1);
arms.note: an assignment used as a value keeps its target fresh, so `all = xs = [1]` leaves `xs` unshared though `all` holds it

arms.name: M-REACH-LAST-STATEMENT-VALUE
arms.replace: final climbs: Bool = true || kind == shape.blockStmtKind
arms.note: every construct a statement ends is climbed as if its value were discarded, so `all = { xs = [1]; }` keeps `xs` unshared

arms.name: M-REACH-DISCARDED-BODY
arms.note: a loop's body is not taken as discarding its last statement's value, so a fresh write ending a loop body makes the local shared

arms.name: M-REACH-DISCARDED-STATEMENT-BRANCH
arms.note: no statement branch or nested block is climbed, so a fresh write ending an `if` / `switch` statement branch makes the local shared

arms.name: M-NULLITY-ALIAS-TRUSTED
arms.note: a typedef proves non-null by being one, so `typedef MaybeR = Null<R>` reads as a plain nominal again

arms.name: M-NULLITY-UNDERLYING-TRUSTED
arms.replace: if (_nominalKinds.contains(t.kind) || t.isAnonStruct || t.underlyingRaw != null) return NonNull;
arms.note: an abstract proves non-null whatever it wraps, so one over `Null<R>` is trusted

arms.name: M-NULLITY-TYPE-PARAMS-IGNORED
arms.find: if (head == null || hops > MAX_HOPS || typeParams.contains(head)) return Unproven;
arms.replace: if (head == null || hops > MAX_HOPS) return Unproven;
arms.note: a type parameter of the declaration a hop reaches resolves to whatever same-named type is in scope, so `typedef Id<T> = T` borrows class `T`'s proof

arms.name: M-NULLITY-BINDING-PARAMS-DROPPED
find: if (typeName == null || isTypeParamAt(typeName, bindingFrom)) return Unproven;
arms.note: the type parameters in scope at a binding are not, so `m<R>(x:R)` borrows class `R`'s proof

arms.name: M-NULLITY-UNRESOLVED-PROVEN
arms.note: a name that resolves to nothing is proven by the empty agreement

arms.name: M-NULLITY-GUARD-IGNORED
arms.note: a `#if`-guarded declaration answers for every branch, though the index kept only one

arms.name: M-NULLITY-HOPS-CUT
arms.note: no alias or underlying type is followed, so an alias of a class or an abstract over one proves nothing

arms.name: M-NULLITY-ANON-REFUSED
arms.note: an anonymous-structure typedef proves nothing, though a structure value is non-null under null safety

arms.name: M-NULLITY-SCOPE-LOST
arms.note: names resolve from no file, so an imported class stops proving anything

arms.name: M-PROVER-NULLITY-SKIPPED
arms.note: the null-safety arm trusts any declared nominal again, so a typedef of `Null<…>` is rewritten by every null-aware check

arms.name: M-VALUE-TYPE-UNINIT-FIELD
arms.note: a value-typed field with no initialiser keeps the fast path, though it reads null on a dynamic target until assigned

arms.name: M-VALUE-TYPE-FIELDS-REFUSED
arms.note: every value-typed field loses the fast path, an initialised one and one read through its getter included

arms.name: M-BINDING-ALIAS-BLIND
arms.note: an import alias never binds its alias name, so a same-package class answers for `import other.Opt as MaybeR`

arms.name: M-BINDING-UNINDEXED-IMPORT-FREE
arms.note: an import or alias of a module nothing can read is taken to declare nothing, so it falls through to the package tier

arms.name: M-BINDING-UNINDEXED-MODULE-FREE
arms.find: if (split.rest.length > 1 || (!aliased && split.rest.length == 1 && split.rest[0] != name)) return Pass;
arms.replace: if (split.rest.length > 1 || (!aliased && split.rest.length == 1 && split.rest[0] != name) || (!aliased && split.rest.length == 0 && SourceText.lastSegment(split.module) != name && !tables().modules.exists(split.module))) return Pass;

arms.note: every report-scope write-index ask builds again

arms.name: M-INDEXSCOPE-HOST-IGNORED
arms.find: return plugin is SymbolIndexHost ? cast plugin : null;
arms.note: no ask reaches the run host: every rule builds its own index again

arms.name: M-INDEXSCOPE-RESOLUTION-OWN-BUILD
arms.note: the resolution question without a scope builds a second report index instead of sharing the memoised one

arms.name: M-SCOPE-UNPARSED-UNSPELLED
arms.note: a library module that does not parse is unknown even for a name its text never spells, so any import of one makes every name unknown

arms.name: M-EXPOSED-WRAPPER-IGNORED
arms.note: a `@:publicFields final class` exposes nothing, its meta sitting on the `final` wrapper

arms.name: M-TS-INFER-SHIFT
arms.note: a call that skips an optional parameter binds a function's type parameter by argument POSITION, so `f(?n:Int, x:T, ?y:L)` called `f(s, u)` takes `T` for `L`

arms.name: M-TS-OVERLOAD-OWN-PARAMS
arms.note: an `@:overload` signature declaring its own `T` agrees with the class's `T` by text, so the call returns the class's type argument

arms.name: M-VALUES-IMPORTED-CTOR
arms.note: an import that puts an enum in scope brings none of its constructors, so a bare pattern naming one reads as a capture

arms.name: M-VALUES-WILDCARD-CTOR
arms.note: a wildcard over an enum brings its statics only, never its constructors

arms.name: M-VALUES-ALIAS-WHOLE-MODULE
arms.note: an alias of a module's main type brings the constructors of every type of the module

arms.name: M-VALUES-FIELD-IMPORT-TYPES
arms.note: a static-field import of a module the index does not hold may bring any value, not just its one field

arms.name: M-MACRO-VALUE-UNLISTED
arms.note: no import of a bare call name is ever out of the index's sight, so a macro an unindexed static import brings is folded into

arms.name: M-MACRO-EXTENSIONS-ONLY
arms.note: a call on a value receiver is taken to be routed by a static-field import of its member name, not only by a `using`

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-LITERAL
arms.find: return if (literalType != null && literal != null && !spellsAnotherType(node, literalType, shape))
arms.replace: return if (literalType != null && literal != null && false)
arms.note: a literal types as nothing, so `'x'.ext()` has an unresolved receiver

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-CONSTRUCTED
arms.note: a construction `new T()` types as nothing in the deep walk

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-ABSTRACT-THIS
arms.note: `this` inside an abstract is the abstract, not its underlying value (4.3.7 types it as the underlying)

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-SOURCE-CALL
arms.find: final receiver: Null<String> = expressionNominalWalk(callee.children[0], root, shape, declaredTypes, index, file, chain, [], true);
arms.note: the source mode reads no method call's return

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-RETURN-TYPEPARAM
arms.note: a return written as a type parameter the call binds is answered verbatim (`T`)

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-RETURN-AGREE
arms.note: declarations writing the return differently answer the last one read

arms.name: M-ELEMENT-PEEL
arms.note: a container under a nullable wrapper has no element

arms.name: M-OUTER-PATH-PEEL
arms.note: a path under a nullable wrapper is the wrapper's

arms.name: M-CONSTRUCTION-CTOR-GAP
arms.note: the constructor's arguments are read as the type's

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-LOCAL-INIT
arms.note: a local written with no type has none, though Haxe gives it its initializer's

arms.name: M-TS-RETURN-WRAPPER-BOUND
arms.find: final written: Null<String> = targetReturnSource(recv, call, currentType, nullableWrappers);
arms.replace: final written: Null<String> = [for (w in [targetReturnSource(recv, call, currentType)]) if (w != null && !nullableWrappers.contains(NominalTypes.outerNominalOf(w.trim(), g._plugin.typeSyntax) ?? '')) w][0];
arms.note: the wrapper refusal reads the return after its type parameters are bound, so a T bound to Null<X> names nothing

arms.name: M-VOCAB-UNION-DUPLICATES
arms.find: if (g != null) for (k in g) if (!out.contains(k)) out.push(k);
arms.replace: if (g != null) for (k in g) out.push(k);
arms.note: a kind two seams both name is answered twice, so every derived set carries a duplicate where the grammar's seams overlap

arms.name: M-VOCAB-UNSET-SEAM-ADDED
arms.note: a single seam the grammar leaves unset adds an empty kind name instead of nothing

arms.name: M-BLAMES-BASENAME
arms.note: the compiler's errors blame any file whose basename they mention: a same-named file elsewhere, a warning, a badge-prefixed line all revert what they name by name only

arms.name: M-BINDER-NAMED-FN-NO-STEP-OUT
arms.note: a rename anchored on a named function expression's own name sweeps only that function's body, though the name binds in the enclosing one

arms.name: M-VOCAB-NESTED-NO-NAMED-FN
arms.note: the named function expression drops out of every nested- and function-like-kind reader: its scope, parameters, returns and captures are read as the enclosing function's

arms.name: M-REWRITE-NAME-CAPTURE-HOLE
arms.note: a NAME-slot capture is handed to the paren guard as a hole again, and since `new (A)()` parses as a call of an identifier `new`, `new $C()` comes back as `new(A)()`

arms.name: M-REWRITE-TRAILER-UNALIGNED
arms.note: one template is spliced unchanged over a statement and a value match of the same `try` pattern, so a `;`-terminated template leaves `;;` after every value site (Haxe: Expected }) and a bare one costs the statement its `;`

arms.name: M-PATCH-OWN-DOC-UNSEARCHED
arms.find: if (located.error == null || occurrences(slice, oldText, kind) > 0) return { located: located, base: groupSpan.from };
arms.note: a fragment widened over the addressed declaration's own doc block is "not found" again, so the doc-orphan refusal's remedy works only through the enclosing type and a type's doc needs comment-rewrite

arms.name: M-PATCH-DOC-OWNER-WRAPPER-BLIND
arms.note: the doc-orphan guard reads a declaration's name off its nameless FinalDecl wrapper, drops the watch, and a typedef inserted ahead of a documented `final class` takes its doc at rc 0

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-IGNORED
arms.note: extract-method --member falls back to the local closure, so the run stays inside the function it was meant to leave

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-STATIC-LOST
arms.find: final isStatic: Bool = shape.staticModifierKind != null && host.run.exists(m -> m.kind == shape.staticModifierKind);
arms.note: a run taken out of a static function becomes an INSTANCE member, which the static caller cannot call

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-COPIES-ASSIGNED
arms.note: a local the function assigns is passed by value, so a write a closure makes while the run calls it no longer reaches the copy the extracted member reads

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-WRITTEN-TYPE-TRUSTED
arms.note: the parameter copies a written type its reads do not have - `?o:String` is passed as `String` while the body reads `Null<String>`

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-MEMBER-TYPE-PARAMS-BLIND
arms.note: a host with type parameters is extracted from, and the member's parameter `w:T` names a type parameter the new member does not declare

arms.name: M-COND-NAMED-FN-NOT-IN-EFFECT
arms.note: a named function literal's name is no declaration in effect, so renaming `v` of `final h = function v() …` past which an arm declares `v` too is not refused and the build that compiles the arm out reads a name that no longer exists

arms.name: M-COND-CONTINUATION-NOT-IN-EFFECT
arms.note: a continuation declarator (`var a = 1, v = 2`) is no declaration in effect, so renaming `v` past which an arm declares `v` too is not refused

arms.name: M-SITES-EXPR-RETURN-NO-LANDING
arms.note: only the `return` STATEMENT lands its value, so an expression-bodied `function f():String return d;` converts nothing and the `toString` it runs is never reached

arms.name: M-MATCH-ONE-FLAT-RUN
arms.find:
final pTypes: Int = pattern.typeArgCount;
		final iTypes: Int = input.typeArgCount;
arms.replace:
final pTypes: Int = 0;
		final iTypes: Int = 0;
arms.note: type and value arguments are one flat run again: `new $C($a, $b)` binds the TYPE arguments of `new Map<String, Int>()`

arms.name: M-MATCH-UNWRITTEN-DROPPED
arms.note: a match on type arguments the pattern did not write is not recorded, so `rewrite` drops `<Int>` from `new Box<Int>(1)`

arms.name: M-REWRITE-UNWRITTEN-IGNORED
arms.find: for (m in accepted) for (part in m.unwritten) return Err(unwrittenRefusal(source, part));
arms.replace: for (m in accepted) for (part in m.unwritten.slice(0, 0)) return Err(unwrittenRefusal(source, part));
arms.note: `rewrite` splices over a construction whose type arguments no metavariable holds, dropping them

arms.name: M-STAR-ONE-PER-LIST
arms.find: if (stars(kids, 0, split) > 1 || stars(kids, split, kids.length) > 1) return TWO_STARS_REFUSAL;
arms.note: `new $T<...>(...)` is refused again although its two stars sit in two runs

arms.name: M-CONDBRANCH-TYPE-ARGS-DROPPED
arms.note: a node the branch projection rebuilds loses its type-argument count

arms.name: M-VALUES-MODULE-WITHIN
arms.note: a use binds the first module-level declaration of the name, whichever #if branch it compiles in

arms.name: M-VALUES-MODULE-ALTERNATIVE
arms.note: a declaration of a branch the use is an alternative of is still one it may bind

arms.name: M-VALUES-IMPORTS-WITHIN
arms.note: a module-level declaration inside #if hides the imported static in the builds without it too

arms.name: M-VALUES-IMPORTS-POSITION
arms.note: the use's own #if branch is not read: a guarded declaration never hides the imported static

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-VALUE-TYPED
arms.find: return values.decls.length == 1 && values.imported == null ? typeSources[values.decls[0].span.from] : null;
arms.note: a module-level value every build compiling the read declares is not typed

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-VALUE-MEMBER-FIRST
arms.note: a module-level value outranks a member the enclosing type's chain declares

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-RECEIVERS
arms.note: a call on a module-level value only some builds declare dispatches on none of its types

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-RECEIVERS-IMPORTS
arms.note: the builds compiling no module-level declaration of the name do not dispatch on the imported static

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-RECEIVERS-MEMBER
arms.find: imported == null || values.decls.length == 0 || CallGraphKeys.memberMayBind(g, currentType, name))
arms.note: a module-level value is dispatched on where a member of the enclosing type's chain may be meant

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-RECEIVERS-UNTYPED
arms.replace: if (nominal == null) continue; if (nullableWrappers.contains(nominal)) return null;
arms.note: a build whose value is not typed is dropped instead of leaving the receiver unresolved

arms.name: M-GRAPH-IMPORTED-POSITION
arms.note: an import binds a name whose module-level declaration every build compiling the read declares

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-CALL-UNSEEN
arms.note: a bare call some builds make on a module-level value holding a function records only the imported static it may run

arms.name: M-SUBTYPE-ARGS-SUBSTITUTED
arms.find: return [for (a in up) CallGraphNames.substituteTypeParams(a, params, args, typeSyntax)];
arms.note: a chain climbing a generic type passes the argument in that type's terms, not the subtype's

arms.name: M-SUBTYPE-ARGS-ARITY
arms.note: a link filling fewer parameters than the type it names has still answers

arms.name: M-MEMBER-KIND-IGNORED
arms.note: a member of any kind counts as one of the kinds asked, so a field reads as an enum constructor a bare call may build

arms.name: M-LANDING-TYPE-ARGS-AS-VALUES
arms.find: for (k in node.typeArgCount ... node.children.length) land(node.children[k], null);
arms.note: a construction's type arguments land as values of no known type: a string conversion of any object at every `new Box<Int>(…)`

arms.name: M-MATCH-TYPE-SLOT-UNRECORDED
arms.note: a match on a type the pattern did not write is not recorded, so `rewrite 'final $x = $v' 'var $x = $v'` drops `:Float` from `final f:Float = 1`

arms.name: M-CARRY-OWN-SUB-UNCARRIED
arms.find: final ownSub: Null<String> = ownSubModuleImport(dep, wanted, provider, cursorInfo);
arms.note: a sub-module type of the source module is carried by no statement, and the move refuses with "no import to carry" over a type `import <module>.<Sub>;` names

arms.name: M-CARRY-OWN-SUB-PRIVATE
arms.note: a `private` sub-module type, which no spelling imports, is carried as `import <module>.<Sub>;`

arms.name: M-ACCESS-GRANT-PER-MEMBER
arms.note: two moved members needing private access each carry their own copy of the same `@:access` line

arms.name: M-KEEP-BARE-IGNORED
arms.note: `--keep-bare` leaves the callers bare with no `import Dest.*;` to bind them

arms.name: M-KEEP-BARE-CLASH-BLIND
arms.note: an identifier of the source spelling another destination static is not seen, and the wildcard may rebind it

arms.name: M-KEEP-BARE-NOT-MAIN
arms.note: a destination that is a sub-module type takes `import <module>.*;`, which imports the main class's statics, not its own

arms.name: M-OWNED-FIELDS-OFF
arms.find: : ownedFieldClosure(srcDecl, srcTree, srcSource, called, destHit.decl, destSource, trees, plugin);
arms.note: the fields only the moved group reads stay behind, and the move refuses as "shared mutable state"

arms.name: M-OWNED-FIELD-ANY-READER
arms.note: a field a staying member also reads moves with the group, and the staying reader routes through the via field unasked

arms.name: M-OWNED-FIELD-ACCESS-BLIND
arms.note: a field reached as `this.x` outside the group moves anyway, and that access no longer compiles

arms.name: M-OWNED-FIELD-PROPERTY
arms.note: a property moves with the group while its accessors stay behind

arms.name: M-OWNED-READERS-UNNAMED
arms.note: the mutable-field refusal no longer names the staying members that keep the field

arms.name: M-RECEIVER-ROUTING-OFF
arms.note: receiver-qualified callers of a moved instance member are left unrewritten, and the next compile reports `has no field`

arms.name: M-RECEIVER-UNKNOWN-ROUTED
arms.note: a receiver of no known type is read as someone else's, so a `Dynamic` holding the source keeps calling a member that left

arms.name: M-RECEIVER-UNRELATED-ROUTED
arms.note: a receiver of an unrelated type declaring a same-named member refuses the move instead of being left alone

arms.name: M-VIA-PRIVATE-REACHED
arms.note: a caller in another class is routed through a private holding field it cannot reach

arms.name: M-COND-ALTERNATIVE-REGIONS
arms.note: two regions spelling the same condition where the earlier branch is taken are never alternatives, so a use in the other's #else may bind a declaration no build compiling it has

arms.name: M-COND-ALTERNATIVE-SPLIT
arms.find: if (earlyChain.length != early.branch + 1 || lateChain.length != late.branch + 1) return false;
arms.note: a chain is split on every | it spells, so a condition holding || is read as a run of conditions it is not and two branches some build compiles together read as alternatives

arms.name: M-GRAPH-BODY-SPLIT
arms.note: a further body of a module-level function folds into the first: every build's code is one node

arms.name: M-GRAPH-BODY-EXPAND
arms.note: an edge naming a module-level function reaches its first body only, never another build's

arms.name: M-GRAPH-BODY-EXACT
arms.note: an edge a bare use binds to one body per build runs every other body too

arms.name: M-GRAPH-BODY-TARGETS
arms.note: a query naming a module-level function answers its first body only

arms.name: M-GRAPH-BODY-COPY-IN
arms.note: an edge an earlier file left on a module-level function never reaches the further bodies its own file declares

arms.name: M-GRAPH-BODY-PURGE
arms.note: a further body keeps the copies of the function's edges from other files when its file leaves, and gets them twice when it is read again

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-BINDING
arms.note: a bare call of a module-level function is bound by name, never per build: module-level code's is unresolved

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-BINDING-MEMBER
arms.note: a module-level function comes before a member of the enclosing chain of its name

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-BINDING-VALUE
arms.note: a build declaring a module-level value calls nothing the graph is told of

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-BINDING-IMPORTS
arms.note: the builds declaring no module-level function of the name call no imported static

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-REF
arms.find: final module: Null<ModuleBinding> = bareModuleBinding(name, arg.span, currentType);
arms.note: a module-level function read as a value is bound by name: one under #if in several builds is no reference at all

arms.name: M-GRAPH-MODULE-IDENT
arms.find: final module: Null<ModuleBinding> = bound != null && bound >= 0 ? null : moduleBinding(name, span, currentType);
arms.note: the one module-level function a bare call binds does not type the call's result

arms.name: M-SUBTYPE-ROOT-NEGATIVE-LIST
arms.note: the root refusal is the negative list it replaced (typedef alias, plain abstract), so a `@:forward enum abstract` over a type reads as provably unrelated to it

arms.name: M-RECEIVER-STRUCTURE-LEFT
arms.note: a receiver of any provably-not-subtype kind is left alone, so a structure value holding the source keeps calling a member that left

arms.name: M-MOVE-OVERRIDE-MEMBER
arms.note: an `override` whose base is outside the scope moves, and the destination declares an override of nothing

arms.name: M-MOVE-IMPLEMENTATION
arms.note: the implementation of an interface method moves, and the source no longer implements its interface

arms.name: M-MOVE-OVERRIDDEN-MEMBER
arms.note: a member a subclass overrides moves, and the override overrides nothing

arms.name: M-MOVE-UNRESOLVED-INTERFACE
arms.note: an `implements` target outside the scope is read as declaring nothing, so a member it may declare moves

arms.name: M-SCAFFOLD-VIA-AT-END
arms.note: the via assignment lands after the last constructor statement again, after a method was bound under Strict null safety

arms.name: M-CARRY-ORDER-MET
arms.note: carried statements land in the order the moved members met them, a `using` between two imports

arms.name: M-CARRY-IMPORTLESS-BELOW
arms.note: a destination with only `using` lines gets the carried imports below its `using` run

arms.name: M-CARRY-USING-UNUSED
arms.find: if (methods != null && !sites.calledThrough(imp.raw, methods, declSpan.from, declSpan.to)) continue;
arms.note: a `using` whose extensions the moved code calls none of is carried anyway

arms.name: M-CARRY-USING-ORDER-MET
arms.note: the union of the members' carried `using` lines keeps the order the members met them in, not the source's, and the extension ranking flips

arms.name: M-BINDER-EXTENSION-ATUSING
arms.find: final own: ExtensionStep = typeStep(receiver, receiver, name, []);
arms.note: the receiver type's own and inherited @:using are skipped, so a file's using answers a call 4.3.7 binds to the type's extension first

arms.name: M-BINDER-EXTENSION-LAST-USING
arms.note: the FIRST using of the file is tried first instead of the last

arms.name: M-BINDER-EXTENSION-FIRST-PARAM
arms.replace: case Misfits: Bound({ members: [m], host: host });
arms.note: an extension whose first parameter rejects the receiver is taken although the compiler passes it over

arms.name: M-BINDER-EXTENSION-UNINDEXED
arms.note: a using the index cannot read is passed over, though it may declare the extension

arms.name: M-BINDER-EXTENSION-GUARDED-USING
arms.note: a #if-guarded using that may supply the extension answers in every build, though without the flag an earlier one binds

arms.name: M-USING-HOSTS-MODULE
arms.note: a used module brings only its main type's statics, not every type's

arms.name: M-USING-HOSTS-ALIAS
arms.find: final host: Null<ResolvedType> = hostOf({ file: fi, type: declared[k] }, []);
arms.replace: final host: Null<ResolvedType> = { file: fi, type: declared[k] };
arms.note: a used alias reads as bringing no statics, though the type it names brings them

arms.name: M-USING-DECLS-AMBIENT
arms.find: for (group in fi.ambientImports) for (i in group.imports) if (i.kind == ImportKind.Using) out.push(i);
arms.note: the ambient import.hx usings are not in scope of the resolver's shadow check

arms.name: M-VOCAB-CONDITION-LOOP-KEEPS-FOR
arms.note: the condition loops keep the iterating `for`, so an empty `for (x in items()) {}` passes as a drain loop

arms.name: M-UNUSED-PRIVATE-CHAIN-BUILD-IGNORED
arms.note: an ancestor under @:build / @:autoBuild counts as fully indexed, so a member its macro may add or read is proven absent and the subclass's private method is deleted

arms.name: M-PURE-STRING-METHOD-OFF
arms.note: a String method on a String final is not pure, so the dead `CHARSET.toUpperCase()` constant stays undeletable

arms.name: M-LOWER-CAMEL-FIRST-ONLY
arms.note: only the first capital is lowered, so `URLLoader` names its value `uRLLoader`

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-BUILT
arms.note: a candidate type a build macro may give the static is read as its declarations, though in that build it binds the call

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-PASS-OVER
arms.note: a candidate type offering no static of the name stops the walk instead of leaving the call to the next one

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-TWO-HOSTS
arms.note: the types of a used module are tried in declaration order, though 4.3.7 tries the last declared first

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-GUARDED-HOST
arms.note: an extension on a #if-guarded type is taken in every build, though without the flag the next candidate binds

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-GUARDED-MEMBER
arms.note: a #if-guarded extension static is taken in every build, though without the flag the next candidate binds

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-STATIC
arms.note: an instance method of a used type is taken as the extension, though a using offers statics only

arms.name: M-EXT-DECL-NOUSING
arms.note: a @:noUsing static is taken as the extension, though 4.3.7 passes it over

arms.name: M-ALLOW-REACHING-FILE
arms.find: for (hit in hits) if (reachesMember(hit, member, owner))
arms.note: every @:allow in the file reaches every member again - a grant on one member taints its neighbours

arms.name: M-CONFINED-GRANTS-IGNORED
arms.note: the confinement proof asks the file-level @:allow answer even when the member's own grants are known

arms.name: M-ALLOW-GRANTEE-SUBTYPES
arms.find: for (sub in index.subtypes.subtypeDecls(t.name, fi.file)) if (!files.contains(sub.file.file)) files.push(sub.file.file);
arms.note: a grantee's subtype, which the compiler also lets in, is left out of the edit set

arms.name: M-ALLOW-GRANTEE-PACKAGE
arms.note: a package grant reaches no type of its package

arms.name: M-ALLOW-GRANTEE-UNMATCHED
arms.note: a grant naming no type the index sees is read as reaching nothing, and the rename goes ahead

arms.name: M-CONFINED-NO-OWNER-FILE
arms.note: a namesake type's subtypes unconfine a private member

arms.name: M-XREN-QUALIFIED-PATH-UNREAD
arms.note: no dotted path is matched against the qualified spellings, neither a VALUE `pkg.T` nor a receiver `pkg.Mod.CONST`

arms.name: M-XREN-SHADOWED-ROOT-BLIND
arms.note: a dotted path rooted in a LOCAL that spells the package (`final p = {C: 1}; p.C`) is renamed as the type

arms.name: M-XREN-GRANT-UNREAD
arms.find: for (arg in children) add(grantOffset(source, arg, typeName, paths.grant));
arms.note: no access grant is renamed, so `@:access(p.Sub)` keeps granting a type that no longer exists - and compiles

arms.name: M-XREN-GRANT-MODULE-PATH
arms.note: a grant is matched by the MODULE path, which the compiler grants nothing for, so a sub-module type's `@:access(p.Sub)` is left behind

arms.name: M-XREN-GRANT-ANY-META
arms.note: every metadata argument spelling the type's path is renamed, a forwarded FIELD `@:forward(R)` included

arms.name: M-XREN-THROUGH-IMPORT-UNREAD
arms.find: add(throughOffset(source, span, importedPath(node, source, refShape), paths.absolute, typeName));
arms.note: an import whose path runs THROUGH the type (`import p.C.K;`, `import p.C.*;`) or an alias import's path is left on the old name

arms.name: M-XREN-THROUGH-NO-DOT
arms.note: an import through a LONGER name the type's path prefixes (`import p.Cx.K;`) is cut as if it ran through the type

arms.name: M-XREN-ALIAS-NAME-READ
arms.note: an alias import is read by its ALIAS, so its path keeps the old name

arms.name: M-LIFT-FINAL-WRAPPER-SKIPPED
arms.find: final lifted: Null<QueryNode> = wrapper ?? (parent == null ? null : literalWrapperOf(node, parent));
arms.replace: final lifted: Null<QueryNode> = parent == null ? null : literalWrapperOf(node, parent);
arms.note: a `final class` addressed through its form is not lifted: `--before` splices between `final` and `class`, a removal leaves the `final` behind

arms.name: M-SORTED-ORDER-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an unsorted list is accepted and entries land between elements in no order

arms.name: M-SORTED-DUP-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an entry already present, or given twice, is inserted again

arms.name: M-SORTED-ANY-CONTAINER
arms.note: a call's arguments or any other container are 'sorted' into

arms.name: M-SORTED-NO-CONCAT
arms.note: a concatenated entry - the spelling of an over-wide one - is no constant string, so a pin list refuses every insert

arms.name: M-SORTED-UNSORTED-ENTRIES
arms.note: entries sharing a gap keep the order they were given in, so `['b', 'a']` into an empty array stays unsorted

arms.name: M-SORTED-SPLITS-DOC
arms.note: an entry lands between the next element and its doc, which then documents the entry

arms.name: M-REMOVE-COMMA-LINE-KEPT
arms.note: removing a one-per-line element leaves its indentation and line break behind, a blank line inside the list

arms.name: M-WALK-LAMBDA-PARAM-CUT
arms.find: host.loopElement(from, ctx) ?? (parameter == null ? null : parameter(from, ident, ctx))
arms.note: the shared walk never asks a host for an untyped lambda parameter

arms.name: M-STD-EFFECT-FREE-AS-TRANSPARENT
arms.note: an effect-free stdlib call counts as transparent, so extract-repeated-expression hoists one `StringTools.iterator(s)` for three loops (the first drains it) and one `Date.now()` for three clock reads

arms.name: M-STD-SPLIT-TRANSPARENT
arms.note: `s.split(",")` counts as transparent, so three calls are hoisted into ONE mutable array shared by every former call site

arms.name: M-STD-SHADOW-IGNORED
arms.note: a project type named `Std` passes for the std one, so its arbitrary `Std.int` is hoisted and a dead store of it deleted

arms.name: M-RETAIN-SOURCES-KEEPS-ALL
arms.note: nothing is ever dropped, so a --fix run keeps every superseded and speculative parse for the rest of the run (the N25 self-fix OOM at the default heap)

arms.name: M-RETAIN-SOURCES-DROPS-LIVE
arms.find: final keep: Map<String, Bool> = [for (source in live) source => true];

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-MEMO-SOURCE-BLIND
arms.find: if (known != null) return known.source == source ? known.visits : record();
arms.note: a tree asked about with another source is answered from the recording made over the first

arms.name: M-NULLFLOW-MEMO-NOT-FORGOTTEN
arms.note: forget keeps the recording, so a pass that re-reads a superseded tree replays it and the memory N36 releases stays held

arms.name: M-HELPER-THIS-KEPT
arms.find: edits.movedTextEdits.push({ span: hit.span, text: hit.interpolated ? '$$${edits.param}' : edits.param });

arms.name: M-HELPER-MEMBER-UNQUALIFIED
arms.note: a moved body's bare read of a member staying on the source is left bare instead of `<param>.x` / `Src.x`

arms.name: M-HELPER-NO-GRANT
arms.note: a moved body reading a private member of the source gets no `@:access` grant

arms.name: M-HELPER-FIELDS-TRAVEL
arms.note: the fields only the moved methods touch move into the static helper as instance fields, although the methods read them through their parameter

arms.name: M-HELPER-CONSTANT-STAYS
arms.note: a private constant only the moved members read stays behind on the source

arms.name: M-HELPER-TYPE-STAYS
arms.note: a private type only the moved code names stays in the source module, where the helper module cannot see it

arms.name: M-HELPER-TRAVELLING-IMPORTED
arms.find: final travels: Bool = travelling != null && travelling.contains(ref.name);
arms.note: a type travelling with the move is still priced as a dependency to import, and the carry refuses it as unreachable

arms.name: M-HELPER-CALL-ORDER
arms.note: call rewrites inserting at one offset are pushed outermost first, so `a.self().add(1)` comes out with its heads swapped

arms.name: M-HELPER-SUBTYPE-CALLERS-SKIPPED
arms.find: final subtypeError: Null<String> = subtypeBareCallers(edits, indexes, calls);
arms.note: a subtype's bare call of an inherited moved member is left calling a member its supertype no longer declares

arms.name: M-HELPER-ARM-RETARGET-NONE
arms.note: an arm addressing a moved member is not reported for retargeting

arms.name: M-HELPER-ARM-STALE-NONE
arms.note: an arm whose find the rewrite changed is not flagged

arms.name: M-HELPER-ACCESSOR-ALLOWED
arms.note: a property accessor moves into the helper, where `<param>.p` calls the accessor it used to implement

arms.name: M-HELPER-FIELD-ALLOWED
arms.note: an instance field is not refused for what it is

arms.name: M-HELPER-MODIFIER-ALLOWED
arms.note: a `dynamic` / `macro` member moves into a static helper, which keeps neither meaning

arms.name: M-HELPER-VALUE-USE-ALLOWED
arms.find: if (placed == null || open < 0) return valueUse(edits.prep.srcTypeName, m.name, where(file, source, offset));
arms.replace: if (placed == null) return valueUse(edits.prep.srcTypeName, m.name, where(file, source, offset));
arms.note: a moved member passed as a function value is rewritten as though it were called

arms.name: M-HELPER-SUPER-ALLOWED
arms.note: a `super` access is not refused for what it is

arms.name: M-HELPER-UNRESOLVED-ALLOWED
arms.note: a name nothing in scope binds is left as it is, though it may be a member of a supertype the index cannot see

arms.name: M-HELPER-SHARED-TYPE-ALLOWED
arms.note: a private type the staying code names too is not refused for what it is

arms.name: M-HELPER-PARAM-CLASH-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a parameter name the moved code already spells is taken, and the local shadows it

arms.name: M-HELPER-GENERIC-ALLOWED
arms.note: a generic source moves with a parameter type missing its type parameters

arms.name: M-HELPER-NON-CLASS-ALLOWED
arms.note: an abstract's member moves into a helper, where `this` is no longer its underlying value

arms.name: M-HELPER-RECEIVER-VALUE-ALLOWED
arms.find: if (open < 0) return valueUse(edits.prep.srcTypeName, h.m.name, where(h.file, source, h.at));
arms.replace: if (false) return valueUse(edits.prep.srcTypeName, h.m.name, where(h.file, source, h.at));
arms.note: a moved member reached through a receiver as a function value (`this.f.bind(1)`) is rewritten as though it were called

arms.name: M-HELPER-MODULE-VALUE-ALLOWED
arms.note: a module-level value of the source module is not refused for what it is

arms.name: M-USING-MEMBER-FIRST-OFF
arms.note: a `.method` access the `using` provably takes no part in counts as an extension use again

arms.name: M-MEMBER-BINDS-STATIC
arms.note: a static of the name reads as shadowing the extension

arms.name: M-MEMBER-BINDS-GUARDED
arms.note: a member under `#if` reads as binding in every build

arms.name: M-MEMBER-BINDS-HOST-GUARDED
arms.note: a declaring type under `#if` reads as declaring the member in every build

arms.name: M-STD-MEMBER-STATIC
arms.note: a static std member reads as an instance one

arms.name: M-STD-MEMBER-VIA-GUARD
arms.note: a std member reached through a guarded typedef reads as unguarded

arms.name: M-STD-MEMBER-ANY-CANDIDATE
arms.note: one std module of a simple name proving the member is enough

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-DECL-TYPE-DROPPED
arms.note: a moved declaration initializer loses its declared type, so a constant whose value is no bare literal reaches the destination untyped

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ALWAYS-BARE
arms.note: the source never gains the import, so a reference from another package names a type it cannot see

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-WILDCARD-IGNORED
arms.note: a same-package reference relies on the bare name although a wildcard import of the source may shadow it

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-NEVER-INLINE
arms.note: a scalar literal moves into a plain static final, so a parameter default it replaces no longer folds

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ALWAYS-INLINE
arms.note: every constant expression is made inline, beyond what inline-constant proves the compiler folds

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ALWAYS-PUBLIC
arms.note: a constant the enclosing type keeps for itself is exported

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-SHARED-IGNORED
arms.note: an array literal moves into one shared static instance without the caller asserting that no reader mutates it

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ANY-AGGREGATE
arms.note: an array literal holding a non-constant element moves as a constant

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-READS-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an expression reading a local is refused only as a non-constant, without the name it reads

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-META-POSITION
arms.note: a metadata argument becomes a constant reference, where the metadata needs a literal

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-CASE-PATTERN
arms.note: a case pattern literal becomes a reference, which the match reads as a capture or a constant of another kind

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-PARAM-DEFAULT
arms.note: a parameter default is replaced by a constant that does not fold

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-SHADOW-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a local named like the receiving type takes the new reference

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-REBIND-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an import or type of the source that binds the receiving type name takes the new reference

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-ANY-HOST
arms.note: an interface or other non-class type is handed a static final

arms.name: M-EXTRACT-TO-UNSEEN-TYPE
arms.find: final unseen: Null<String> = request.dest == null ? null : firstUnseenType(declType, plugin);
arms.note: a declared project type travels into a module that may not see it

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-DOC-STAYS
arms.find: final from: Int = ElementSpan.docExtendedSpan(source, spanOf(moved[0]), regions, true).from;
arms.note: the slice leaves its first element's doc behind, where it documents the next element

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-RANGE-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a range past the array moves a shorter slice than asked, or none

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-READS-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an element reading a local moves where that local does not exist

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-UNSEEN-TYPE
arms.find: final unseen: Null<String> = crossModule ? ExtractConstantTo.firstUnseenType(element, plugin) : null;
arms.note: an element naming a project type moves into a module that may not see it

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-NESTS-UNCHECKED
arms.note: a slice is moved into its own array

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-TARGET-POSITION
arms.note: a target position is resolved after the cut, where it points at other code

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-SOURCE-UNVERIFIED
arms.note: a source that did not lose exactly the slice passes the check

arms.name: M-MOVE-ELEMENTS-ORDER-UNVERIFIED
arms.note: an append that lost the slice order passes the check as a multiset

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-MAIN-SHIFT
arms.find: return index < own && !mayShift(g, id, index, count);
arms.note: an argument a skipped optional may shift onto a later parameter is taken at its written position

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-MAIN-SIGNATURE
arms.note: a call two signatures may answer is taken to bind each argument at its position

arms.name: M-TS-SPAWN-ARG-POSITION
arms.find: { index: i - first, count: args.length - first }
arms.note: an argument position counts the callee child too

arms.name: M-LAYOUT-SPLICE-BYPASSED
arms.note: a format-preserving grammar's edits are spliced raw, so an entry appended to a one-per-line JSON array lands as `, x` on the previous line

arms.name: M-COMMA-CONTAINER-KINDS-UNREAD
arms.note: a sole entry has no adjacent `,`, and the container kind is no longer asked, so an insert after it is joined by a newline instead of a `,` and the result does not parse

arms.name: M-BINDING-EITHER-DROPS-REST
arms.note: a guarded statement's candidates leave out what the builds without it bind

arms.name: M-BINDING-EITHER-DROPS-GUARDED
arms.note: a guarded statement's candidates leave out what the statement itself binds

arms.name: M-BINDING-EITHER-OPEN-READ
arms.find: mine == null || theirs == null ? Unreadable(null) : Either(mine.concat(theirs))
arms.note: the other builds' binding nothing reads is dropped from the candidates instead of leaving them open

arms.name: M-BINDING-CANDIDATES-OWN-TYPE
arms.note: a name the module declares itself is given the candidates its imports bind, although its own type outranks them

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-LOCAL-CONSTRUCTION
arms.note: a local written with no type and initialised by a construction stays untyped

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-INITIALIZER-ONE-STEP
arms.note: a local initialised by another local that holds a construction stays untyped

arms.name: M-ADDMETA-SAME-ARGS
arms.note: a duplicate is judged by the entry NAME again, so a second `@:access(...)` with another argument is refused although Haxe allows several

arms.name: M-ADDMETA-ENTRY-NEVER-SAME
arms.note: no entry ever equals the one being added, so the exact repeat of an annotation is added a second time

arms.name: M-SLOTS-FIT-SKIPS
arms.find: if (p.optional && !p.rest && fit != Fits) step(walk, arg, param + 1);
arms.note: an argument that fits an optional parameter may also skip it, so `f(?a:Int, ?b:String, c:Int)` called `f(1)` reads as binding `c`

arms.name: M-SLOTS-MISFIT-BINDS
arms.note: an argument binds a parameter it misfits, so `g(true)` keeps `true` in `?a:Int` as well

arms.name: M-SLOTS-MAYFIT-BINDS-ONLY
arms.note: an undecided fit only binds, so the way the compiler skips the parameter is lost

arms.name: M-SLOTS-MANDATORY-MISFIT
arms.note: a mandatory parameter an argument misfits is skipped, so a call that cannot compile reads as binding the next one

arms.name: M-SLOTS-UNBOUND-MANDATORY
arms.find: for (p in param ... params.length) if (!params[p].optional && !params[p].rest) return;
arms.note: a run leaving a mandatory parameter unbound is kept

arms.name: M-SLOTS-REST-ONCE
arms.note: a rest parameter takes one argument only

arms.name: M-SLOTS-OVERFLOW-PARTIAL
arms.note: past MAX_RUNS the runs found so far are answered as all of them

arms.name: M-TS-AFFIX-USINGS-UNCHECKED
arms.find: if (declares) return { path: path, hosts: hosts.types };
arms.note: a later `using` declaring the affix method itself is passed over, so its guard is decided by StringTools

arms.name: M-WALK-ARITHMETIC-OFF
arms.find: final arithmetic: Null<(node:QueryNode, operands:Array<T>, ctx:C) -> Null<T>> = host.arithmetic;
arms.replace: final arithmetic: Null<(node:QueryNode, operands:Array<T>, ctx:C) -> Null<T>> = null;
arms.note: arithmetic is untyped by the shared walk

arms.name: M-REACH-HOMES-RECORDED
arms.note: a placeholder records no type it stands for, so a name several declarations share loads none of them and the walk refuses as code it did not read

arms.name: M-REACH-LIBRARY-HOMES
arms.note: an external node loads its type by simple name alone, which several declarations of it leave unread

arms.name: M-REACH-ONE-TYPE-PATHS
arms.note: (soundness) types of two packages sharing a simple name answer as copies of one type

arms.name: M-REACH-ONE-TYPE-FOLDED
arms.note: (soundness) a copy inheriting the member, whose code no declaration of the node is, answers through the other copies' bodies

arms.name: M-REACH-ONE-TYPE-EXTERN
arms.note: (soundness) an extern copy's target code is taken to run nothing of the program, an override below it included

arms.name: M-REACH-SHARED-ONE-TYPE
arms.note: (precision) copies of one type on two class paths stay a name two types share

arms.name: M-REACH-UNREAD-NAMED
arms.find:
case Opaque:
						return AliasedUnread(file, shared, id);
arms.replace:
case Opaque:
						return Aliased(file, shared, '', new Span(0, 0));
arms.note: library code the walk cannot read is refused as code at no file, naming no member

arms.name: M-TYPING-ANSWER-FORGOTTEN
arms.note: a remembered answer is computed again on every asking: the table keeps nothing

arms.name: M-TYPING-KEY-FILE
arms.note: a member question is keyed by the declaration's offset alone: a namesake at the same offset of another file takes its answer

arms.name: M-TYPING-KEY-OFFSET
arms.note: a member question is keyed by the file alone: two types of one module share one answer

arms.name: M-TYPING-TYPE-KEY-FILE
arms.note: a type question is keyed by the declaration's offset alone: a namesake at the same offset of another file takes its answer

arms.name: M-CG-DISPATCH-MEMO-LEAKS
arms.note: the dispatch memo outlives the edges it was kept for: a query after a file is taken out answers the overrides read before

arms.name: M-CG-DISPATCH-MEMO-BY-TYPE
arms.note: the dispatch memo keys by the receiver type alone: the first member dispatched on a type answers for every other

arms.name: M-ANCESTOR-ARGS-OFF
arms.find: for (a in above) CallGraphNames.substituteTypeParams(a, params, args, _typeSyntax)
arms.note: what a link passes is not substituted for the ancestor's parameters, so a chain answers the ancestor's own parameter names in the start's terms

arms.name: M-ANCESTOR-SHORT-ARGS
arms.note: a link writing fewer arguments than the parameters it fills still binds them, to nothing written

arms.name: M-UNIFY-CHAIN-OPEN
arms.note: a class whose whole chain resolves without reaching the other type is undecided instead of refuted, so no plain argument skips an optional parameter

arms.name: M-UNIFY-ALIAS-STOP
arms.note: a plain alias is not followed, so a type reached through one is never decided

arms.name: M-UNIFY-GUARDED-PLAIN
arms.note: a declaration under `#if` is decided as if one branch were every configuration's

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-OPTIONAL-PARAM
arms.note: an optional parameter reads as its written type, not the optional value the compiler types it (`Null<T>`)

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-UNREADABLE-WRITTEN
arms.note: a written type that is no one type (`#if` inside it) is answered verbatim

arms.name: M-MEMBER-OPTIONAL-READ
arms.note: an optional structure field reads as its written type, not `Null<T>`

arms.name: M-MEMBER-READ-HOST-ARGS
arms.note: no argument binds the declaring type's parameters, so a member written with one is unknown everywhere

arms.name: M-INDEX-OPTIONAL-FIELD
arms.find: return decl != null && decl.kind == kind && decl.name == member.name || meta != null && metas.contains(meta);
arms.note: a structure field written `?a: T` or `var ?b: T` is not optional, only one under `@:optional`

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-RETURN-PARAM-NAME
arms.note: a method returning a type parameter answers the parameter's name as a call's nominal

arms.name: M-STRUCT-READONLY-INVARIANT
arms.note: a read-only structure field asks for the same type, so a subtype refutes a structure the compiler unifies with

arms.name: M-STRUCT-MUTABLE-SAME-DECL
arms.note: a mutable structure field compares types by simple name, so a namesake of another package conforms

arms.name: M-NOMINAL-SELF-PARAMS
arms.note: a generic type's `this` is its bare name, so a member written with its own parameter reads as nothing off `this`

arms.name: M-UNIFY-GENERIC-GIVEN
arms.note: a given type with type parameters is undecided against a plain wanted type, though its chain alone decides it

arms.name: M-EXT-TYPE-USING-FORWARD
arms.note: a type's @:using paths are tried in written order, though 4.3.7 tries the last written first

arms.name: M-EXT-INTERFACES-FIRST
arms.note: the inherited @:using lists are tried in written order, so an interface written before the superclass comes first

arms.name: M-EXT-ALIAS-STOP
arms.find: return next == null ? Open : typeStep(next, receiver, name, seen);
arms.note: a typedef receiver stops at its own @:using, though 4.3.7 goes on to the aliased type's

arms.name: M-EXT-MODULE-FIELDS-OPEN
arms.find: return hosts.moduleFields.exists(f -> f.name == name) ? Open : Passed;
arms.note: a module-level function of a used module is passed over, though it may be the extension the call binds

arms.name: M-EXT-NULL-PARAM-OPEN
arms.find: return args.length == 1 ? writtenFits(receiver, args[0], m, host) : MayFit;
arms.note: a `Null<T>` first parameter is undecided, though it accepts a `T` receiver

arms.name: M-EXT-DYNAMIC-PARAM-OPEN
arms.note: a `Dynamic` first parameter is undecided, though it accepts every receiver

arms.name: M-EXT-ITERABLE-ELEMENT
arms.note: an Iterable over a concrete element accepts every iterable receiver, though only one of that element binds

arms.name: M-EXT-FIELD-FIRST
arms.note: an extension answers a name the receiver's own type declares, though the field binds first

arms.name: M-EXT-AMBIENT-FIRST
arms.note: the ambient import.hx usings are tried before the file's own

arms.name: M-EXT-PRIVATE-OPEN
arms.note: a private static is taken as the extension from any file, though it is reached from its class and its subclasses only

arms.name: M-UNIFY-SELF-OPEN
arms.note: a declaration the cast graph reads as no end (an anonymous structure) is undecided against itself, though `unify` starts with `a == b`

arms.name: M-EXT-AMBIGUOUS-MODULE
arms.note: of a module the index holds in two files, one file's candidate is taken though the compiler may load the other

arms.name: M-EXT-GUARDED-LINKS
arms.find: if (step != Passed) return t.guarded ? Open : step;
arms.note: a supertype one #if branch of the receiver's type writes answers for every build

arms.name: M-ADDIMPORT-STATEMENT-KEYWORD-IGNORED
arms.note: a whole `using x.Y;` statement is added as an IMPORT of x.Y — the keyword the caller wrote is read and then ignored

arms.name: M-ADDIMPORT-USING-TAKES-IMPORT-SEAT
arms.note: a fresh `using` takes the import ladder again, which for a using-only header appends it BELOW the group: top static-extension priority, re-targeting the calls the file already makes

arms.name: M-ADDIMPORT-PATH-UNCHECKED
arms.note: text that is no module path reaches the splice and is refused as a parse error at a column of a source the caller never wrote

arms.name: M-IMPORTSPELLING-FLAG-CONFLICT-UNCHECKED
arms.note: an `import x.Y;` statement under --using is silently taken as one of the two requests instead of refused

arms.name: M-REMOVEIMPORT-KEYWORD-IGNORED
arms.note: a `using a.B;` request matches the `import a.B;` beside it too, so the keyword that names one statement reads as ambiguous

arms.name: M-LIT-QUALIFIED-KINDS-IGNORED
arms.note: the import kinds a caller asks to widen are carried and never read, so a dotted import or using is blind to a simple-name query

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-TAB-ROW
arms.note: a tab-aligned row (`@param\tname\t\tdescription`) is reflowed and its continuation lands at the bare gutter under none of the columns

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-CODE-SHAPED

arms.name: M-COMMENT-REFLOW-SPLITS-CODE-SPAN
arms.note: a space inside a backtick span becomes a break point, so an inline code sample is split across two lines

arms.name: M-LITERAL-WRAPPER-SKIPPED
arms.find: final lifted: Null<QueryNode> = wrapper ?? (parent == null ? null : literalWrapperOf(node, parent));

arms.name: M-LITERAL-STRANDED-ACCEPTED
arms.note: a lifted literal that is not a whole list item is removed anyway instead of refused

arms.name: M-UNIFY-ABSTRACT-OFF
arms.note: an abstract on either side is undecided again, so its clauses never decide a unification, a static extension's first parameter or a read-only structure member

arms.name: M-UNIFY-CAST-TRANSITIVE
arms.note: a clause of an abstract that is not transitive allows a second abstract cast, so `B` reaches `Top from Mid` through `Mid`'s own clause

arms.name: M-UNIFY-CAST-STACK
arms.note: a cycle of transitive clauses is walked forever instead of answering MayFit

arms.name: M-UNIFY-CORE-WIDENS
arms.note: two different core value types never unify, so `UInt`'s `to Int` no longer reaches `Float`

arms.name: M-CASTS-BRANCHES-AGREE
arms.note: one `#if` branch's clause decides for every build, so an abstract casting from `B` in one branch only takes `B` everywhere

arms.name: M-CASTS-MEMBERS-OFF
arms.note: an argument's cast reads no `@:from` / `@:to` member, so a conversion member never binds a parameter

arms.name: M-CASTS-FIRST-FROM
arms.find: either(inwardMembers(given, wanted), firstClause(wanted, b -> b.from, t -> castPath(t, given, stack)))
arms.note: the cast stops at the wanted abstract's own members and never casts to its first `from` clause

arms.name: M-CASTS-FIRST-ONLY
arms.note: the LAST clause unequal to the abstract is cast to instead of the first, so `Ad from Dz from Bs` takes a `String`

arms.name: M-CASTS-CORE-ABSTRACT
arms.note: no core value type is an abstract, so a `Bool` argument takes the arm of a class and casts on through the wanted abstract's first `from` clause

arms.name: M-CASTS-GRAPH-PARAMS
arms.find: return r.type.typeParamArity > 0 ? null : graphWith(r, t -> writtenEnd(t, r, at, []));
arms.replace: return graphWith(r, t -> writtenEnd(t, r, at, []));
arms.note: an abstract with type parameters gets a graph, its clauses read without the arguments that bind them

arms.name: M-CASTS-TYPE-SELECTED
arms.note: a `@:multiType` abstract, whose cast the compiler picks by its type arguments, is decided by its clauses

arms.name: M-CASTS-HAND-UNIFIED
arms.note: an abstract the compiler unifies by a hand-written arm (`EnumValue` takes every enum) is decided by its empty clauses

arms.name: M-CASTS-MEMBER-CERTAIN
arms.find: final certain: MemberInfo -> Bool = m -> single && !m.guarded;
arms.replace: final certain: MemberInfo -> Bool = m -> true;
arms.note: a conversion member under `#if`, or of a type two branches declare, casts in every build

arms.name: M-CASTS-BUILD-OPEN
arms.note: an abstract a build macro may give a conversion member is read as having none

arms.name: M-CASTS-DYNAMIC-END
arms.note: a clause writing the dynamic type is no end the graph models, so `Any` (`from Dynamic`) takes nothing

arms.name: M-ANCESTOR-DEFAULT-FILL
arms.note: a left-out argument is filled with the parameter's own name instead of its default, so `Box` reads as `Box<T>`

arms.name: M-ANCESTOR-DEFAULT-MISSING
arms.note: a left-out parameter with no default is skipped instead of refused, so a reference the compiler rejects gets a spelling

arms.name: M-ANCESTOR-COMPLETE-OFF
arms.find: if (decl == null || args.length >= decl.type.typeParamNames.length || decl.type.name == _bareType) continue;
arms.note: no reference is completed, so a written `Box` stays `Box` where the compiler reads `Box<Int>`

arms.name: M-ANCESTOR-BARE-TYPE
arms.note: the dynamic type written bare is treated as a reference leaving its parameter out, so it has no answer

arms.name: M-ANCESTOR-SCOPE-OFF
arms.find: if (filled == null || seen.contains(key) || scope.contains(path) || unspellable) return null;
arms.replace: if (filled == null || seen.contains(key) || unspellable) return null;
arms.note: a name a type parameter may hold is completed as the type of that name

arms.name: M-ANCESTOR-DEFAULT-VISIBLE
